product_name: Rocketfish Universal Wireless Rear Speaker Kit RF-WHTIB-A
review_text:
I'm unable to run wires to my rear speakers, so I have been looking for a wireless solution. I purchased the Rocketfish wireless rear speaker kit at BB and was pleasantly surprised by the quality given the many negative reviews of this unit. I'm by no means an audiophile but the speakers I have plugged in sound crystal clear to me. One thing to note is the unit will add a bit of latency to the audio (the nature of wireless), so you will want a receiver capable of correcting this or the audio coming from your rear speakers will have a slight delay. The auto calibration feature on my Onkyo receiver detected the additional latency and corrects for it. I can't even tell the speakers are connected wirelessly.

I have the transmitter placed about a foot from my dual-band (2.4ghz and 5ghz) wireless router. I get absolutely no audio interference. The receiver is placed about 10ft away from the transmitter.

product_name: Analogix Semiconductor SP1004 Slimport to HDMI Adapter for Amazon Fire, Blackberry Passport, Nexus 5, LG G3
review_title: My SP1004 was unstable. With a HDMI shielded cable, works fine, but apparently only 720 HD
review_text:
The SP1004 unit that I received is faulty. It transmits video with its audio, but every 3 or 4 minutes the signal is lost for a few seconds and then the transmission recovers. So the device is basically useless to do what I intend to do which is turning my LG G3 into a media center for videos.

The representative from (Demandport? or Analogix) says that:
"To ensure you have a genuine Analogix Slimport SP1004, there are several conditions that must be met, among others:

- The adapter itself must have "Full HD" printed on it.
- The packaging must indicate that it is an SP1004."

And that: "Demandport is the sole distributor of original Slimport products."

My SP1004 unit complies with the conditions of being "authentic" because it has "Full HD" and "SP1004" printed, and because I indeed bought the device from Demandport. And in spite of that, I got a defective adapter.

I'm located outside the U.S., so for me, returning the unit is actually more expensive than buying another one from scratch! So I'm bound to try a lucky shot by buying another SP1004 from Demandport, and I expect that this time the unit will be OK and just work flawlessly.
If the second one also comes faulty, I expect a full refund for both units, or at least two SP1004 devices that work perfectly, no matter if I have to spend even more money sending the devices to the location in the U.S.

Update for 2017: Fortunately, I did not threw away my unit because recently, I decided to give it a try just out of frustration. And... surprise! It worked and wasn't unstable! The radical difference was that this time I used a top quality hdmi cable, which is probably shielded inside. It turns out that the device connected to my LG G3 is very sensitive to electric noise. One additional comment: The quality of the transmitted image appears to be 720HD. I was expecting full HD (1920x1080) because the LG G3 phone has a 2K screen. Can anyone clarify what's the actual definition of the transmitted video?

product_name: Sony CMTX5CD Powerful NFC Bluetooth Speaker with CD Player
review_title: Good sounding bluetooth speaker with lots of features
review_text:
Pros: good sound quality, good build quality, sleek design, ease of use, included remote control, Songpal app
Cons: good (but not amazing) sound quality, small display faces upward and not easily visible unless standing over the product, remote control required for full access to the device menu

I ordered this for casual music listening in bedroom/office. I wanted a small, unobtrusive speaker system with bluetooth capability and good quality sound. I also wanted a remote control, which is not very common in this category - other products included the Fluence Fi30 as well as 'portable' systems like Jawbone Jambox, Oontz, etc. The Bose, B&W, and Sonos products were above my price range.

The X5CD is a very good product and serves my needs perfectly. It appears to have good build quality. It sounds very good and low and medium volumes and is certainly sufficient for a medium sized bedroom. It has user-selectable equalizer presets, custom equalizer option, and a few digital sound processing presets (e.g. can mimic wide soundstage). After trying several combinations, I found that the Sony suggested preset called CA+ sounds best to my ears.

Bluetooth pairing was simple and bluetooth streaming audio quality was good. The product supports AptX and AAC codecs for improved streaming sound quality.

The remote control is small but contains all the functions. Conveniently, the remote's battery is pre-installed. Note that the remote control is REQUIRED to access the menu of the X5CD. Also, the X5CD can be controlled with the free Sony Songpal app from your iphone/android - the app can replicate most functions of the remote and the app can control the X5CD as long as it's already paired via bluetooth. Using the Songpal app for adjusting the equalizer and settings is far easier than using the remote and navigating through the menu via the small display.

The X5CD has a small display on the top of the unit. Unfortunately this display can only be seen when the user is standing directly over the device, as the display faces upward. product_name: Merci Finest Selection
review_title: The sun sure didn't have any mercy on these.
review_text:
I don't eat a whole lot of chocolates any more, but when something new comes around, I give it a shot.

Quick note- the chocolates arrived to me with over half of them melted, being reduced to half the size of their individual plastic wrapped sizes. It wasn't a pretty sight when I opened the mailing envelope and saw chocolate oozing from the sides of the box.

Of the batch, my favorite was Praline Cream. I've never had this before and when I took a small bite from the piece, I was hooked and took out the rest of it, and the second one in no time. All the others...to be honest, were pretty plain. If I hadn't read the wrappers or anything on the box, I wouldn't have really known what it was that the others were supposed to be. Most of them tasted like regular chocolates to me. Granted, at this price point, you can't expect anything extravagant or mind blowing, but it sure isn't the "finest" Europe has to offer by any stretch of the definition. And some of this might be because of the whole melting thing. Either way, I wasn't that impressed.

If I ever get around to buying another box of these, and they aren't melted and I end up liking them, I'll update this review. Until then, I just see this as a basic chocolates in a fancy cigar box-looking presentation. Well, melted cigars anyway.

product_name: Harman Kardon Aura Wireless Stereo Speaker System
review_title: Great sound, amazing design, but hindered by weak firmware and companion app.
review_text:
This unit sounds great and looks amazing. I'd like to give it a few more stars, but it suffers from a few key issues - there are some rough edges on the firmware on the unit itself, and general weirdness in the phone app used to control/configure the device. Wouldn't be a big issue in a $200 product, but for something that retails for $400 bucks, you'd hope they'd have the kinks worked out.

Notes:
- I love the all-in-one design of the Aura. An elegant one piece unit nearly eliminates cable complexity and fills the room with full and rich sound.
- If you're going to use this as an AirPlay speaker, there doesn't seem to be a way to enter the password for wifi network. The only way to do it seems to be to have it copy the settings from your phone. It worked with my iPhone, but it seems clunky.
- The iPhone app is pretty useless aside from initially configuring the wireless.
- The Aura is about 30 ft from my router, joined to a 802.11g network. It holds the connection and streams well 95% of the time, but can sometimes disappear from the AirPlay on both my phone and desktop iTunes. This is probably less of an issue with the device than it is with the AirPlay protocol itself.
- The controls and indicators on the device could be better. The power and volume buttons are touch-sensitive, but don't give any sort of feedback, so I'm always left wondering if the command I just tried to give it has registered.
- I don't have the same concerns about Bluetooth pairing that the other reviewers mention, but I could see how this would be an issue for you if you lived in a dense apartment building.

Bottom line:
It's great if you can set it and forget it. But if you use it primarily as an AirPlay speaker, you'll have to fiddle it every once in a while when it drops the connection. When that happens, you'll be annoyed that the process isn't a little smoother in something you paid $400 for. Without a firmware update and a new version of the companion app, it's a reasonable value at $300, a steal for $250, but overpriced at $400.ion of the companion app, it's a reasonable value at $300, a steal for $250, but overpriced at $400.

Our farmers send their cows out into lush, organic pastures for fresh air, exercise and grazing (weather permitting of course). Supplemental organic grains can include any of the following: corn, soy, oats, barley, triticale and other small grains. Animals also receive necessary mineral supplements that sometimes include non-iodized salt.

I'm very disappointed and won't buy again but will go back to Pure Indian Foods Brand which is more expensive though.

product_name: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_title: A great little music player, as long as you're not looking for heavy/deep bass...
review_text:
Let me start by saying this little music player does sound fantastic with the right equipment. The customizable EQ allows for the mids and highs to be very audible and crisp. The bass is also there, but even with the low frequencies maxed out on the EQ, its not as deep as I would like, but this is just personal preference. Everyone has different hearing to some degree and prefer different EQ's. The audio quality this device can deliver is very respectable. With over 11,000 reviews averaging 4-5 stars, its obvious this player suits the needs of most people.

I like how this device can deliver a flat signal for music, which I find useful for the line-in application to my computer, which already has my customized EQ for increased bass and highs and reduced mids for the type of music I prefer. This is the only way I am currently using this player for now.

In comparison to the [[ASIN:B003JME32C Cowon J3]] (one of the best-sounding music players to date, unfortunately, it seems to have been discontinued), even with bass amplification from the [[ASIN:B005HJWWW8 Fiio E6]], the bass for the Clip+ is noticeably deeper but not as heavy as the Cowon J3 without amplification. This is the only thing I found most disappointing about the player for my own personal needs.

For the record, I prefer to listen to music with [[ASIN:B00HYH7HXA V-Moda LP2]] Over-ear headphones and [[ASIN:B001LNO722 Monster Turbine]] In-Ear buds. I wouldn't put these up against high-end professional sound equipment, but they're capable of amazing sounds compared to the crappy ipod buds I see a lot of people walking around with. I believe the Dr. Dre line of products are also capable of great sounds, but I don't think they're as durably constructed as V-moda.

The features for this player are perfect for the purpose it serves: Listening to audio. It doesn't have anything extraneous that it wasn't designed for, and it comes in such a compact package. The expandable memory slot is an added feature that I find to be genius. This player does a lot right and nothing wrong. If It was one thing I'd ask for in perhaps a "Clip+ 2" version, it'd be a bluetooth feature.

I would recommend this player to friends and family as long as they're not all about the bass...

product_name: Lisse 8-Speed Facial Brush Skin Care Cleansing System Kit, Pink
review_title: Is this some kind of sick joke?
review_text:
Okay, so I'm actually super mad about this. Amazon, you talked up Prime Day like it was the second coming of Christ, and then you give me this! THIS! This cleansing system is "marked down" from $99. Like, don't make me laugh, Amazon. I could have made a better cleansing brush with an ordinary household sponge taped to a drill.

On Prime Day, this bad boy was 20-something bucks. Not bad, I thought. All the other Prime Day deals consisted of baby toys and 20% off Planters peanuts. I freaked out when I saw this! I mean, I thought I was saving a lot of money!

I ordered it and was super excited. Two days later, the package comes. I open it, and the box was all fancy, so I was thinking, "I can get down with this." Anyway, I open it and start inspecting. The big brush was pretty soft and seemed nice. The other brushes weren't that impressive. I was disappointed. Then, I tried to open the battery compartment. Now, I know it says "batteries not included" in the description. And I knew that going into this mess. Well, I wrestled with the battery compartment for what felt like three hours until it finally snapped open. At this point, I've lost about fifteen pounds because it is on so freaking tight. You'd think they were keeping the Krusty Krab secret formula inside or something. Well, it opened. No batteries, of course, like, I knew that. All I am saying is that this brush is originally $99, yet they can't include batteries? Okay.

So, I was reading the instructions, which seem pretty impossible to understand. I'd like to think of myself as a well-read, educated gal, but I couldn't understand them. I don't understand how this brush has eight speeds when it only has an on and off button but okay. I'll take their word for it. It's really hard to figure out how to order replacement heads; I'm not even sure that my instructions came with that part because I couldn't find it anywhere.

As I was inspecting the other brush heads, I picked up the pumice stone thinking, "Yeah, buddy, my feet are gonna be lovin' this!" Just as that thought crossed my mind, the pumice stone fell off of the brush head and onto my lap. I kid you not! I didn't even touch it! Like, I wasn't playing around with it or anything. I think it fell off when I picked it up. As if it was just glued onto it with Elmer's glue or something, not even super glue. Just Elmer's. So, that happened. It was sitting in my lap, and I just started laughing. Why would it be so easy to just knock off like that? This product is "worth" $99! You'd think it would have been super glued at least. It's not!

At this point, I've already decided to send it back. But that isn't even the best part. I take the little brush head off, and I try to put on the big soft brush head just to see how to change the brush heads. The little one comes off pretty easily. I pop on the big one and lock it in place. Okay! Nice, nice. Well, then, this thing gets stuck! The big brush head got stuck onto the base and would not come off. How weird is that? Why wouldn't they make it easy to come off? If I am using this in the shower, and I have wet and soapy hands, I don't want to fight my brush head to come off. I want it to come off real easy. I don't wanna play games; I wanna get clean.

Needless to say, I was pretty disappointed with this overall product, and I just wish it was made better. I know I got it for 20-something dollars, but now it's back up to almost fifty bucks, and that isn't fair. Because people are going to spend $50 on this dollar store face cleansing brush, and they're going to be really disappointed!

So, just take my word for it! If you're looking for a brush that "is as effective as systems sold by skin professionals for nearly $200," please look somewhere else. This is not that face cleansing brush. I get better results from my $15 Neutrogena Microdermabrasion System.

product_name: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E3416 Magnetic Elliptical Trainer, Gray
review_text:
I bought mine through walmart but the people need to know. AT 6' tall, I was worried about stride length and so I found 4 different stride estimates for this machine on other websites. One said 13" another said 11-15" another said 16" and another said 18". I managed a decent HIIT workout on a friend's 12" so I figured I wouldn't have an issue with this one. At the very least, I thought that I could still get a decent pre-workout warm-up out of this and it did make me sweat but the pedals angle downward so much that my toes jam into the front of the pedal base and I can't lean back and concentrate the movement into the back of my legs. With feet stuck all the way forward, the stride length feels shorter than friend's 12". I feel all the burn in the top of my knees/bottom of thighs. Stacking some of those foam puzzle floor pieces under the front of the machine helps me lean back a bit but this wasn't the worst issue.

The worst issue was the lack of resistance. Notch 1-7 feels like zero resistance and notch 8 feels like a little more than zero resistance. It was like pedaling a bicycle after the chain falls off. If anyone knows how to manipulate resistance or jury-rig it, please let me know. Also, the LCD display lights up but doesn't work. Duct-taped a dollar store digital kitchen timer over the LCD screen

review_text:

product_name: Gavina 100% Columbian, Ground Coffee Portion Packs, 42 Count
review_title: Amazingly good for coffee out of a can.  Locally roasted here in So Cal.
review_text:
I'm amazed.
My coffee obsession is such that I buy and roast my own beans, have been on and off for 20 years. I have most every type of brewer.
When I don't roast my own, I buy Peet's beans locally, there's a Peet's down the street from me.
I hate charcoal burned coffee- people drinking it, is to me a sign that they have no idea what they're doing. Drinking cups filled with hot milk, flavored with a few drops of charcoal coffee. I'm talking about Starbucks, most of what Peets sells, most of what the "craft" roasters make. The Peets blend that I drink is Cafe Solano, what they call "light roast". It is similar to a northern Italian roast, pioneered by Ernesto Illy.
Speaking of Illy, the only canned coffee I would ever consider drinking is Illy Caffe medium roast. I keep a box of Illy medium roast ESE pods around for my espresso machine for extreme emergencies. 100% of the canned coffee in Italy is absolute stale swill other than Illy, so when I travel there, one of the first things I do is buy a few cans. The worst of course is Lavazza. Absolute swill. They brag that "Lavazza is the #1 coffee in Italy". Sure maybe, but you can also say that "Wonder Bread is the #1 bread in America". Not much to brag about.
So, no canned coffee for me other than Illy. Until now. I was at an awards dinner last week, one of the gift bag items was a can of this Gavina espresso. I thought to myself, "uh, huh. probably swill", but I was out of beans over the weekend, so I cracked it open and loaded up the Bialetti moka pot. Holy Arabica Batman, it's not over roasted, it's fresh and aromatic, it's very well blended and nothing sticks out at you to ruin the experience. No charcoal, no wine-y sourness, no aftertaste, etc. Just good coffee.
The first pot was of course the best, when the can was first opened. Now 3 days later it's showing it's age and getting oxidized so I hope I finish it before it gets completely stale.
I hope Amazon starts selling this again.

My major complaint is that it seems to get interference frequently, as it drops the signal whenever I get on my laptop, which means I end up having to move the parent unit to another spot until it stops. Otherwise a very good video monitor at a good price.

However, for $350, they are a good deal.

I have no horse in this race and I do not work for any of these speaker companies. Audio has been a hobby of mine, on and off for 30 + years. My recommendation to anyone looking to purchase is to audition these for yourself as well as some more expensive speakers to see how they differ. That will also reveal areas of weakness. Then, you will be able to determine what is important to you and how much you will need to pay to find something you enjoy.

product_name: 66 AUDIO - BTS+ SPORT - Bluetooth Wireless Headphones - 25+ Hour Battery, Voice Call Noise Cancellation, Stereo Sound
review_text: Overall solid piece of equipment for those of us who don't like cords. I bought this for the wireless, sport style and great reviews. I'm not a runner by any means but find myself in varying situations of physical movement - from a desk to a shop environment. The amount of up and down movement this set allows vs cords is second to none. Not getting caught on something anymore is a magical feeling. I had no interest in the big over the head studio phones for the reasoning of heavy physical movement and price. I can use this set for just over a week straight in 1-4 hour streaks without having to recharge it. It fits comfortably on my head and seals out most sounds pretty well (just ask everyone who's tried to get my attention). The only time it gets moderately uncomfortable is from having only one side hanging on my ear and the other on my neck. Sound quality is great and clear, only lacking in the true bass department. If you push these against your ears for a better seal you'll get the missing bass tones. Connecting these aren't a big hassle either. I use this primarily with my LG G3 & off and on with my laptop. Every now and then you have to go a screen or two into the control panel on the phone for it to transfer all sounds to the headset. The LED indicator light that blinks for any setting is based in one corner and doesn't do a great job of lighting the entire clear section up. Phone calls are about average from what I've been told by those on the other end of the call. The ear pieces are wide and will make you look like Princess Leia, but I wasn't exactly going for looks. It may also take you a few times to figure out where the user control buttons on the right ear piece fall. I've found myself trying to click volume up only to hit skip forward 4 times. I would definitely suggest these to a friend or colleague if they're looking for a headset that will stay on their head no matter how much they move around.

review_title: Honestly one of the best products I have used
review_text:
I don't normally write reviews, but this product (Laneige Lip Sleeping Mask, 20g) was truly extraordinary. Allow me to tell you why this product merrited a 5-star review:

3) It has a soft berry scent, but it isn't strong, and it doesn't taste like anything.

4) A little goes a long way. I cannot stress that enough. Even with a "thick" layer of the stuff on my lips, I barely scratch the surface. I believe that this product will last at the least 6 months of nightly usage.

5) I have used a "thin" layer during the day in liau of lip balm, and it works amazingly.

6) It's a small container, making it perfect for travel as well. Like I said before though, a little goes a long way.

All-in-all, this product is well worth the money, and I will repurchase it once I have finished the first one.

To solve this I tried to use the wired (ethernet) port but could not get it working. That may have been caused by the Gramofon not being able to use my dhcp router, and there did not seem to be anyway of manually configuring it.  Even when using the wired port, it seemed to still need WiFi active in order to set-up or use it with Spotify Connect, so I went back to using WiFi.  In the end I had to move my WiFi access point to within a dozen feet of so of the Gramofon in order for it to start working as I expected it to. Now it works fine - except for when the WiFi network in the house is even a little congested with other traffic.

product_name: Klipsch R6 Black In-Ear Headphone with Patented Oval Tip (Black)
review_title: A musicians take...dont listen to the reviews about too much bass
review_text:
Will try and keep this short and sweet. Don't do a lot of 'reviewing' but for this product, I just had to! Do my fair share of research on most of my purchases, so know how important these reviews can be. For the R6, I found some to be helpful but still lacked in some detail. Here's the deal, I've been a musician for 20 years and I have music in my ears for hours a day, everyday. Like most, I still live on a budget and although I have pricier and more "studio friendly" equipment I use for playing, I wanted something for the day to day, ie, working out, listening at work, etc. The Klipsch R6's fit the bill!

I tend to like a more 'bassy' mix and based on reviews this seemed to be the right product. Let's clear that up. While the Klipsch R6 DOES have a 'bassier' feel, its a lower toned rumble, not the "kick in your ears" I was expecting. Bass is good but certainly not overwhelming. That being said, the thing I do like about the bass mix, is its not muddy. I can still pick up great highs that aren't too "tingy" and good mids.That can be an issue with bassier headphones.

As far as built quality and durability, you wont be let down there. Size and weight are great too. Feel very little ear fatigue, even after hours of wearing them. You will want to take time and see which ear tips work best for you, go too small and you will get frustrated with them falling out during more strenuous activity, not to mention, you wont be getting the full affect of the bass and the noise cancelation (which btw is great).

That's all I got. Would have given 5 stars if the bass gave me more of a kick but other than that, you wont be sorry you made this purchase!

product_name: Summer Infant Digital Color Video Baby Monitor - Dual Coverage
review_title: Unsatisfied With This Monitor Set. Would Not Recommend
review_text:
Unsatisfied. For the price I paid, I could have bought a better set.

1. Flimsy construction and feel. I don't know about you, but when my baby is not sleeping, she likes to play with the monitors. These are not sturdy enough to handle being played with by a baby. The screens are soft. They don't have a hard plastic cover to protect it. So if you press on the screen, the image flexes and the liquid crystal inside shifts around. I don't know why they do this. Never mind a child but honestly it's not sturdy for an adult either. Won't last a month in my house. Plastic is light and brittle feeling. Feels like the kickstand would break off.

2. Screen stays on until you turn it off. This is OK. I'm just not used to it because the other monitor I have by Levana, the screen comes on when the baby cries or moves. And will turn off after a few seconds of inactivity...like if baby falls back asleep by herself

3. Constant streaming audio. This is what I dislike the most. I don't want to be kept up all night with a constant stream of the audio from baby's room. Baby's are noisy sleepers. They coo, wail, gurgle, moan, giggle, and make all sorts of sounds in their sleep. As a mother of a young baby, I am hyper vigilant whenever I hear any sounds so the constant stream of audio coming from this monitor keeps me up all night and I cannot relax. My Levana only comes on when baby cries of moves. That is...both screen and audio. I can even set the sensitivity so I can get some shut eye, and only be awakened when it is actually needed.

4. Night vision picture quality is poor. It's worse than my very basic (cheapest model) Levana which I thought was just OK. But with this one, sometimes I don't even see a baby in the crib. She completely gets blended/blurred with the crib linens.

This set made me appreciate my Levana so much more (Haha). I sent this set back after using for just 2 nights....before I lost any more sleep and before me or my kids break the monitors.or my kids break the monitors.

product_name: Satechi NFC-Enabled Bluetooth Audio Receiver with HD aptX for smartphones, tablets, Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge, S6, S5, S4, Note 3 / iPhone 6, 5, 5C, 5S, 4S, / iPad Air, Mini, 3, and more Sound Systems
review_title: Not Recommended - Issues with Optical Output - Noise Glitches, Audio Mute Problems Cause Frustration - Bad With Pandora
review_text:
Note: Updated to reflect experience found after trying the sister device, Monoprice Bluetooth receiver with APTX support. I have owned both.

I had high hopes for the Satechi Bluetooth receiver, as I use the TOSLINK optical digital output to use with an external digital-to-analog converter (DAC) for great sound quality. I purchased this unit to replace my former Belkin BT HD which worked well and mostly very reliably and also features a TOSLINK optical output but not APTX support.

However, after having tried the Monorprice unit as well as it's companion, repackaged as the Satechi model, I found they share the same frustrating problems. What problems, you may ask?

Note: I use the unit within about 1 ft from my phone and have no nearby Bluetooth units that may cause interference. I do not use the analog stereo outputs, in order to get maximum use out of the capabilities of the receiver.

- Audio dropout (muting) problems: There appears to be a somewhat frequent problem with the beginning of audio tracks losing the first ~2 seconds of sound when playing media, especially when using Pandora. For example, when switching songs in Pandora, the beginning of each song just "dissappears". I have discovered that the sound is being greatly reduced for some reason, and therefore can't be heard momentarily.

This happens very often, although not 100% of the time. Similar with movies and .MP3s, etc. It is as if the unit has sync problems or has muted audio when no signal is momentarily present, and can't catch up correctly when data is sent over Bluetooth. Very frustrating!!

Again, this was not an issue when using my original Belkin HD receiver.

- Random noise problems: There seems to be a random issue with a crackly, grating sound lasting for just a moment that seems appear for no apparent reason at times. No idea why this is happening.

- Sound quality: no complaints; upper frequency range is nice, and I have tested with videos, Apple lossless .M4A files and 320kbps .MP3s as well as .CDA (standard CD) tracks. So far, the APT-X support seems to sound nice and works well.

Unfortunately, I will have to switch back to my Belkin BT HD Bluetooth receiver which did not exhibit the problems listed above and seemed to work well.

If you change media or music fairly frequently, I would recommend you consider other Bluetooth receivers and avoid having to deal with the beginning of your music mysteriously dissappearing. product_name: Herbalist - Vitamin C Serum for Face - 20% Hyaluronic Acid
review_title: Not bad but not my favorite
review_text:
It is not a bad product but it is not my favorite face serum. I've tried a few now and in comparison I'd say this product is just ok. I like that it comes in a dark bottle with a pump and was mostly full but applying it is a little more challenging than others because it is much more liquid-y. The pump takes a couple presses to get started the first time you use it and rotates very easily but getting the serum out is easy enough. It's just that every time you get a drop the serum runs down your finger if you are not quick to get it to your face. You could apply it with a cotton ball but that way you lose a lot in the transfer. For the price point it's good that the serum is completely clear and gets absorbed quickly so you can put it on before makeup but I haven't seen any real results from using this product so while I don't hate it because I don't think anything bad can come from putting vitamin C on my face I'm also not giving it a raving review.

review_text:
Excellent treadmill. Terrible packaging. First treadmill arrived with the plastic case broken. Amazon did promptly send a replacement treadmill and a label to ship it back, but that doesn't change the fact that I had to wrangle a very heavy treadmill around an extra time. The Amazon rep I contacted was on autopilot and didn't read my complaints about the packaging.

I have been using it for a month. The console is kind of stone age to work with, modify settings etc. Would be nice if you could just control it via an app wirelessly, but I get how you have to have a console anyways in case that doesn't work for some people.

The way the belt is arranged it's kind of a pain to lubricate especially with the spray bottle Lifespan sells, but life goes on. Your best bet is to just lubricate the center where you can really lift the belt and then cycle it to spread the lubricant.

This is a long treadmill. It takes up a lot of space which is not desirable for a standing desk where there is really one sweet spot to stand in and that is it. Maybe there is a technical reason for why a long deck is still necessary?

*edit*
I have had this maybe 6 months and have walked hundreds of hours and miles on this Treadmill. The Bluetooth integration is completely non-functional and I can't connect a device. Not a huge deal, but it would have been nice.

The treadmill is also very loud at this point. I think the copious dust and dog hair in my apartment has gotten into the motor causing it to rattle. It doesn't rattle if it is running without me on it. The vibration from my steps messes something up. They don't make an effort to filter the air going into the motor. A few dollars worth of filter could make this thing last longer and run quieter. No way you can use it in a shared space.

The console is still laggy and unresponsive and a pain to work with.

That said I am not changing the number of stars. I have docked the product enough. It works really well at it's core purpose and I enjoy it and would purchase it again if I couldn't find a better option. I love having a treadmill under my desk and it has done wonders for my health and well-being.

review_title: Dentist ordered me to quit using. Turns some folks teeth dark and can might not be reversable.
review_text:
Supplied by orthodontist during brace work. Did not work to prevent canvities a year following brace removal. Negative one.

Negative two is what sent my dentist over the moon. I couldn't understand why I couldn't get rid of the darkening areas of my teeth and when cleaning the hygienist said get off this stuff if you are using it. They continue to sell it but it should be taken off the market. Not all fluride products cause this. Colgates Gem-kal does not. I am switching back to it as my extra fluride prevention now. Something to do with the type of flouride used here and maybe coupled with the inert or other ingredients which are not suppose to be active in purpose but may interact. Not all people experience this but enough that our small town dentist office is alarmed and zeros in on it pretty fast.

Negative one...interesting I was using it after the braces were removed and not prone to cavities at all...14 years here in this town and right where the braces were attached to two teeth probably caused some surface damage and within a year the cavity took place smack in middle of side of tooth. WOW...so much for using this product every day...turned teeth brown and did not protect from cavities...two at least. So this is a warning...and heads up to anyone who might notice the teeth are turning brown or dark and you can't seem to do anything to stop it.

product_name: Chun Zheng Men's Winter Casual Down Hooded Warm Jacket
review_title: Nicely made, good quality materials, but runs VERY small and has a trim cut
review_text:
This jacket has a lot going for it -- great build quality for the price, and a nice, understated overall look. The biggest problem is the fit. This is a jacket for very thin people!

The construction quality is very good -- I was unable to find any loose threads, all seams were tight and even, and the cuffs and waist band are well-made and comfortable. Both the outer material and the lining feel substantial and able to withstand a decent amount of wear and tear. The pockets are positioned for easy access and have good quality snaps to close them. It came tightly bundled up in a package, but it unfolded and plumped up very quickly.

The only so-so item in terms of quality is the zipper. It has nice, chunky teeth, but the pull tab is on the small side, and the entire zipper is plastic.

I like the overall look. It's very simple (solid black) but with a nice contrasting checkerboard lining pattern. The hood is attached and, in an odd design choice, the zipper runs the full length of the hood, so you could, technically, zip yourself totally within the hood.

The biggest problem is the fit. I knew that this would run small, so I got it as an XXL (I normally take either a L jacket if it's dressy, and an XL if I want a more casual, baggy look). Even as an XXL, this is tight in the chest and shoulders. I have a pretty slim build, and I find the fit constraining. This jacket is completely unworkable if you have a good amount of meat on your bones.

The sleeve length is fine, as is the overall coat length. It's just cut for a very, very slim built person even in the XXL size.

It's hard to judge the warmth since it's summer, but the material bulk feels like it would be a fine coat for fall in any climate, and would be OK in winter if you live in a more mild climate.

At this price point, it easily is worth a 5-star rating for construction, 5-stars for material quality, and 5-stars for overall look. However, the fit/cut is a 1 star. Overall rating is 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 given the price point. However, this rating comes with the STRONG caveat that if you're not super slim, don't get this coat even if you size up to XXL.

product_name: World's Best Cat Litter Extra Strength
review_text:
I switched over to WBCL last month and honestly, it's such a nice product. It makes me feel better that its all natural and the most important part is both of my cats love it. No accidents outside of the litter boxes.

I originally started with the red bag (multiple cats, clumping) and it was okay. The litter smelled like corn but after awhile it started to put me off when I scooped the boxes. I tried the LAVENDER scented bag and oh my goodness. Such a difference. I'm not usually a fan of lavender but now I get a whiff and for once Im not disgusted by my cat room.

Scooping the litter is easy and I live on my own land with a private septic so I flush everything. So much easier and with summer coming up, Im so excited that the random fruit flies won't be around. I started with a 15lb bag for two litter boxes and now I just buy the 7lb bags to top them off. It lasts a good amount of time and I feel like I'm not wasting a bunch of litter each week or two weeks. Obviously there is a little dust but not as much as the crystal litter. My favorite part is the fact that I have a very easy routine. I scoop and flush twice a day and that's it. I'm happy and my cats are happy. No more cat litter smells!

I rated it 4 stars bc after a while the lavender scent starts to fade. Adding more litter seems to help a bit but now I'm thinking of picking up some lavender essential oil and adding a few drops from time to time.

Highly recommend this product! You'll actually get excited to scoop litter because of how easy it is!

review_text:
**Pros**
Steak/meaty aroma
Fantastic sized treat
Natural
Dog loves it

**Cons**
None

I've never even heard of these dog chews. I read the directions here on Amazon said to microwave them for 45 seconds. I was very hesitant to do this because it seemed weird. However, it was awesome to watch! the chews come in a nice 1 inch cube then in the microwave they expand to triple their size. I'm sure you can give these to your dog without microwaving them, but I think they'll enjoy them more after they're microwaved.

While they're 'cooking' there's a meaty steak-like aroma that comes from it. It isn't a gross dog food smell. It smells very similar to a microwaved meal. The treat had to taste delicious because my dog felt guilty taking it because he thought it was people food and he isn't allowed people food. After giving it to him it took a few minutes before he realized it was for him and he went over and scarfed it down. He licked up every crumb afterwards, too. When he was done he looked at me and thumped his tail heavily in happiness.

Overall, I think these Himalayan Dog Chews are a fantastic special treat for your dog that I'm sure they'll love. They're natural and have no additives, which is an extra bonus.

product_name: BEST Forehead Thermometer - Non Contact Dual Colour Display - 20 Reading Memory - FDA Approved with Lifetime Guarantee- 5 Star Rated
review_title: We used it on our 3 week old and we've now learned that this device is not recommended for newborns
review_text:
Full disclosure for this review: We used it on our 3 week old and we've now learned that this device is not recommended for newborns. However one of the reasons for the low review is that I feel the age range needs to posted SOMEWHERE on the packaging but instead it is printed in small print in the manual. The box just says "safe for children". In fact on the first page of the manual it states it is "suitable for people of all ages".
That being said, we also tested it on ourselves vs 2 different axillary digital thermometers (both orally and under arm) and the San Sero showed 1.6 and 1.1 degrees higher. If we were talking a difference of 97.1 to 98.6 degrees F, that isn't too large of a number. But when we're talking a difference of 99.4 to 101 F we're now in hospital territory for a newborn. Because of this 101 degree reading our 3 week old was admitted into the hospital, put on an IV, and had multiple tests ran on him to search for an infection that we've no learned did not even exist. This thermometer may be a good purchase for some, but for us we're disappointed in both its readings vs other thermometers and the fact that it is not clearer on the packaging or in the manual that this device is not intended for newborns.

product_name: Kleancolor Nail Polish NEON Colors Lot of 6! Lacquer Neon Collection + Free Earring Gift
review_title: I fell in love with the colors (and the price) online
review_text:
I fell in love with the colors (and the price) online. However, the colors and the quality of the polish do not perform well.

A few things about my relationship with Nail Polish:

- I have 30-50 colors at any given time.
- If a color doesn't look good with my skin color, if I get bored of it, or I notice it doesn't get much play in the rotation, I give it to my nieces.
- I LOVE bright colors. I also love Blues.
- I love opaque polishes.
- I always use base coat and top coat, and usually use 2 coats of color.

So this purchase:

- The Green paints on very, very thin, almost sheer. The first coat makes my nails look diseased. Additional coats didn't do much for color saturation. It was very ugly.

- The Yellow was sheer as well, and despite rolling the bottle before application, the color seemed to pool in the corners. I had to use 3 coats and it just looked too iridescent. I was hoping for a bright Daisy yellow - not a dull Banana or Pale Lemon and this was a mix of both.

- Red, Purple, Blue, Pink - were opaque (as seen in the photo), but the polish is very goopy and takes forever to dry. I make sure that the brush isn't dripping and do 3 simple strokes - side/side/center.

- The Red looks "cherry red" online but the actual color was a pinkish orange. I'd rather it have been a bright NEON orange as the photo suggested.

- The Pink is very pretty.

- The Blue is very summery.

- All colors chip very easily - after only a few hours, and I avoid using my nails as tools, wear non-latex gloves for cleaning, and "baby" my nails for the first 24 hours. I also tried several base and top coats to help prevent the chipping, but found no solution.

I am overall VERY disappointed. If you're looking for something to last a few hours, it might work, but for what I wanted - bright NEON colors that lasted a few days - it was not a good purchase.

product_name: Numi Organic Black Tea, Loose Leaf Tea
review_text:
I'm not a tea expert, but have been drinking for 5+ years now. I'm used to some of the standard nicer green and white teas: Jasmine Pearls and Silver White Needle. I mention this, because the taste of this Gunpowder floored me, compared to the lightness of those other two. I didn't realize that a green tea could taste so heavy. I steeped it under 176 degrees, to avoid the strength of the tannins, but, wow, this had a very smoky flavor. I couldn't rate it down for this, because that may very well be the true flavor of the tea -- I just am not a fan of it. I've purchased the Numi mint, in an attempt to balance out the harshness of this Gunpowder. I've read on another site that blending the two makes a 'Moroccan Mint' -- Numi does label their mint tea with that name, but the ingredients show only mint and no Gunpowder. I hope the mint tea will truly be as "light" and "sweet" as their description claims, in order to counter the overwhelming smokiness. There are mixed reviews on the mint -- very love/hate.

UPDATE 5/29/15
I've received the Numi Mint and I think it is a nice light flavor, that adds a balance to the Gunpowder. I drink the Mint on its own, as well as blending it with the Gunpowder to make the Moroccan Mint. I'm not sure how true to the real Moroccan Mint this is, but it salvages my pound of Gunpowder. product_name: Sennheiser Momentum On Ear Headphone
review_title: A good mix of sound quality, price, portability, features, construction and design sometimes wins
review_text:
I still love my cheapo earbuds but I got tired of having things in my ears all the time. So I wanted to get something portable (on-ear), with iPhone controls and with enough genuine sound quality that I could listen to them all day in the office. I guess comfort would play a role there too.

Very bass forward sound. Great for podcasts, oddly enough. The mids and treble are too recessed to not boost with an EQ. They're nowhere near as present as in my V6s. Thankfully, the treble booster preset on my phone works pretty good at making these things sound balanced. Once properly EQed, they're quite listenable. The detail is pretty good but I've heard better. These are meant to be on-the-go headphone and to that end, they do a great job. The on-ear style doesn't isolate external sounds very well, so the extra bass can be handy when it cuts through the low rumble of my noisy commute.

The build quality is nice. Feels well made with quality materials. Clamping pressure is solid enough to have to keep my eyeglass stems on top of my ears so that they don't get sore. The cable connector is snug and the cable material never tangles or makes noise. The cable with mic and controls is great and really the final reason I chose this set over others. Design wise, they're retro and refined. Cool but not too showy.

If I was over the moon for their sound profile I'd give them 5 stars. From what I've read, the new Momentum On-Ear 2.0 are an audible improvement on this model but these are much cheaper.

review_text:
When I ordered this item from Amazon Vine in early August 2015, I did so "blind," as it were; Amazon at that time featured no product page on this item to describe the specifics. The product link from the Vine listing to offering the product page was then nonexistent.

And so it remained as of this writing on August 12, and so it would appear, until mid September 2015. In all that time, Amazon offered no product of this specific name available at all. A search on Amazon for this item, Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System, came up blank. In fact, a search of the entire internet for this specific item comes up blank.

Needless to say, Amazon listed no product dimensions on the Vine offering page, and no useful details, either.

All of that background should explain this somewhat unconventional report on a product that I did receive, granted, free, in exchange for an honest review.

Here's the description Amazon Vine provided:

"The Bose Solo 15 Series II TV sound system is a one-piece speaker that delivers dramatically better sound than your TV.

"Advanced Bose technologies make each word and detail sound clear at any volume, and create an experience that's wider than the screen. The system also produces impressive bass that adds impact to your shows. And when you want even more clarity, dialogue mode makes every word easier to hear without having to adjust the volume from scene to scene.

"Setup is easy, with just one connection to your TV. The system fits under most TVs up to 50 inches yet is still small enough to place on an open shelf.

"It features Bluetooth connectivity, so you can stream music wirelessly, and includes a universal remote."

That's all I had to go on, so I took a flyer. Alas, the thing proved much too large for our purposes.

The only thing Amazon listed that sounded close to this item was, I assumed, version I, i.e. the original Bose® Solo 15 TV Sound System, although it includes no Roman numeral in its name, And that sounded like it might be workable, at least.

I also assumed, from the photo on Vine page offering the item, that it was much smaller than it in fact is. Alas, it is quite large, as another reviewer I can see as of Setepmeber 24, has also commented. But until very recently there were no reviews visible, since there was no product page.

I had hoped to use this with a 24-inch TV that we use as a computer monitor, and also as our digital TV, but the system is far too large for a computer desk, measuring roughly 28 inches wide. But this thing is not "small enough to place on an open shelf." It is much deeper than all the shelves in our house, about 17 inches deep.

So, Bose, I recommend that you get your product page straight before offering this item to anyone else, and that you also provide some useful information, that is, dimensions, weight, etc. etc.

I don't mind that I can't use the item, as I did not pay for it. I give a completely neutral review, as I also cannot test it. product_name: Micca COVO-S Compact 2-Way Bookshelf Speakers
review_title: About as good as you can do at this price.
review_text:
The Micca Covo S's are an interesting speakers. They have some very good points along with some bad ones, and some that are just so so. I will highlight each of these below.

Just as a provisor, I've only had these speakers for about two days now and I've only listened to them for about three hours. I've also played pink noise through them for about four hours so they've had approximately a seven hour break-in period so far.

The Good
1. NIce design - they are small cube-like speakers that have an attractive, understated appearance. They won't be winning any design awards, but they won't look absurd with most decor either.
2. Five-way binding posts are a welcome and rare feature for speakers this price. They make attaching wires or using banana plugs a snap. My standard double-screw banana plugs fit into them just fine.
3. They really hit low for speakers this size. I was able to get them to hit as low as 60hz, but sound was definitely distorted at this frequency. They sound best with ones 120hz and higher. Still, for a speaker this size, their bass is quite remarkable. I think this is do to the fact that they are rear ported giving their woofer good excursion.

The So So
1. I would put their overall sound quality in the 'so so' bracket. It is still some of the best for speakers in this price and size range. I've definitely heard worse for more money. However, If you go up by $20 to the Dayton B652AIRs you'd notice an obvious upgrade in sound. I have both the B652AIRs and the Covo S's, and I definitely prefer the B652AIRs. Having said this, the Covos are not bad if you only have $40 to spend on a set of speakers.
2. Where these speakers really struggle is in the mid-range frequencies. Voices are muffled and a little distorted. Listening to fiddles, guitars and bag pipes on tracks from Skeryvore is a joy, but once the vocals kick in you can instantly hear the shortcomings of these speakers. Again, I've heard worse, but for just $20 more you can get quite a lot better.
3. The grills are not magnetic! This is not a necessity, but is a very nice feature found on the Micca MB42 and 42Xs. Since it's not a deal breaker I put it in the 'so so' section.

The Bad
1. My main complaint with these speakers is that they can't get very loud without noticeable, and even painful, distortion. I would not recommend them for a room larger than 12'x12'. My pair is connected to a SMSL SA50 amp - which is rated at 50WPC - and they struggle to fill my 20'x15' living room. You an hear them throughout the room, but sound becomes thing the father away you are.
2. As a bit of an ancillary, but still note-worthy, complaint; You have to bee at least a foot away from these speakers for optimal sound quality. Any closer than that and you lose treble and bass is a little embellished. As I write this review they are about 8" from my face and they don't sound as good as when I back up a foot or so. This is definitely something to keep in mind for your application.

So...should you purchase the Micca Covo S speakers? Well, I would say that depends on two factors.

1. What is your budget? If it is just $40 then I'd say "yes." If you can spend just a little more look elsewhere.

2. What is your application? If you plan to use them in a small space where you don't have a lot of extra room and your room isn't too large they will work great. If you have the space and budget I'd definitely recommend upgrading to something like the Dayton B652AIRs or Micca MB42Xs. I've auditioned the MB42Xs and at twice the price of the Covos they are well worth it. They would be my main recommendation for budget hi-fi audio if you have a money and space. They need at least 8" of open space behind them for their rear port to function properly. This is something to keep in mind when choosing speakers for you space.

My plan for the Covos is to use themin my bathroom connected to a Lepai LP-2020A+ amp and an Airplay receiver. The total cost for this system will be just under $90. I wouldn't want to spend too much more than this on a system that will be in such a humid environment. They Covos are a great choice for this application because they are fairly inexpensive, compact and sound good despite their price and size.

THe reason I have given the Covo S speakers four stars is because of their lack-luster mids and inability to play that loud. Stay tuned for further updates on their long-term use.

ONE MONTH UPDATE

I just set these speakers up in my bathroom. I paired them with a Lepai 2020A+ amp and a cheap Airplay receiver. For this application they work great! I did not want to spend a lot of money on a system for my bathroom, but I still wanted decent sound. These speakers fit the bill perfectly! I am very happy with this system overall. The total cost was $78 plus the speaker wire that I had laying around. Much better than any iHome system you could get and about the same price.

FIVE WEEK UPDATE

Even thought It has not been a lot longer I still wanted to share a couple more flaws I've observed as of late.

The first observation I've made is that the Covo S's do best with more acoustically based music. Genres such as jazz and big band really shine on these little cubes offering a nice soundstage with plenty of stereo separation. However, where they really seem to struggle is with rock music that is driven by electric guitars. The guitar tones come off a little muted and even distorted at times. I believe this is due to the size of the these speakers. Most smaller bookshelf speakers - and even some larger ones - struggle to properly reproduce the sound of rock music.

I've also notice that the bass on these speakers sounds a bit strange. I believe that this is due to the fact that these speakers reproduce bass acoustically - meaning, theyuse rear porting and sound echoing rather than relying on large woofers with high excursion. This results in a more boomy rather than tight bass. This more evident in genres such as hip-hop, R&B and dance that have a punch bass track to them.

Despite these newly observed flaws I'm still giving the Micca Covo S's a four star rating. I still believe that they are an excellent value. They really do work well in my bathroom setup filling the room with warm, pleasing sound. Stay tuned for further updates.

Sure, you can get a little IP cam for less money that mostly does the same thing, but I have tried a couple of those and to be honest the phone interface is not as reliable and nicely executed as the Withings interface.  I am really glad I bought these as they have served me relatively well for 3 babies... I would certainly buy another Withings product in the future as I think they really are pretty innovative. product_name: Nestle NIDO Fortificada Dry Milk
review_title: Great backup for fresh whole milk or cream
review_text:
Great shelf-stable milk backup. We have a toddler & go through a lot of milk, but I live in a small rural town, so when I run out unexpectedly, it's inconvenient to drive for it.

This makes a rich, creamy milk, with a nice, fatty (but not greasy) mouth feel. Good for drinking for the kiddo (who wouldn't tolerate toddler formula or other shelf-stable backup options), cooking or coffee. It's especially nice for cooking, since you can mix it richer for creamy applications, whether that's your coffee or a sauce.

It doesn't have the sweetness of fresh milk, and so tastes too flat somehow for me to drink on its own. But it's an excellent fresh substitute in a pinch for everything but adult straight drinking. But it's better than those shelf-stable liquid cartons, so between the two, I'd definitely pick this for the cost and flavor.

product_name: Audio-Technica ATH-MSR7 GM (Gun-Metal Grey) High Resolution Audio Over-Ear Headphone (Japan Import)
review_text:
Was looking for a portable headphone with good sound quality. Picked this over the Sennheiser momentum after a lot of research on the net.

Build Quality 4.5/5
First of all, I must say, I am really impressed by the build quality of this pair of headphones, especially at this consumer price bracket. Everything except the headband are of sturdy build. The brush metal finish is higher quality than the sony mdr-1a, and looks freakin amazing with the red accents. The stock cable is nothing good or bad. Does its job and nothing beyond.

Comfort 3/5
The headband pressure and the clamping force is a real pain (physical) to deal with. I had to bend and twist it to stop it from making a dent on my skull. The earcups are soft and comfortable. However, after an hour of listening or so, they can get a little warm. On a side note, the msr7 is by no means light. I consider it slightly heavy for a portable headphone (when compared with the momentum).

Sound Quality 5/5
The SQ is what really matters most after all, and this pair of cans surprised the heck out of me. The soundstage is very wide and deep for a closed-back headphone. Comparing to my home-use Q701, the soundstage is more defined, and when amped properly, more airy than the q701 although less wide. The Msr7 is definitely bass shy in every way, anyone who cannot live without a good amount of bass should stay away from it. Bass was amazing out of the box, too bad they disappeared after burn-in, but they are still very well textured. Sub-bass extension is mediocre, but mid to upper-mid bass are well done. Upper mids and highs are the real gems here. The clarity and shimmer don't lie to your ears. The amount of details is just absurd with amping. No wonder the high-res tag. Even without amping, with my cowon J3, it reveals decent amount of detail. Although sound isn't completely grain free and smooth like the much lower priced Fostex TH7, the MSR7 doesn't sound harsh to the ears either despite its highs focused signature. In general, I will recommend the MSR7 to female vocals lovers. Whoever listens to Pop and movie soundtracks will be very pleased with the purchase.

Isolation 3.5/5
Isolation is adequate for indoor usage. Just don't bother trying wearing it on the streets. It's not enough for outdoors. It's not a lightweight headphone either and not to mention it gets warm after a while. If sweaty ears isn't your thing, just don't. I guess its a bit of compromise made by ATH for the great soundstage and SQ.

Value 4.5/5
At this price point, I must say the MSR7 has a really high c/p value. You can only turn away from this headphone because of its ridiculous headband, or that bass4lyfe is your life motto. Did not regret my purchase at all.

product_name: LG Electronics LAP240 Sound Plate 100W Slim 4.1 Surround Sound Speaker System with Built-In Sub Woofer and Bluetooth
review_text:
I purchased this LG sound system recently from Amazon as having purchased one of the TV models a few months ago that was listed as compatible I found that while the TV (the 50 inch model) has a spectacular picture but terrible sound. The reason for the poor quality is due specifically to the fact that the speaker has to be mounted on the back of the TV to keep its slim form factor. So while the TV is beautiful to look at all the sound that comes from it is coming out the back speaker and being reflected off the wall back at the listener. It makes the sound seem muted and dull. So again, I purchased this sound plate because the TV can sit on it and come out from all sides of the set.

Of course there has to be a "but" coming up...

But while hook up can be done wirelessly or wired (and it does come with an optical wire) the bass is very deep and tends to drown out much of the spoken work. There are 3 sound settings to choose from but they really sound very much alike.

It is a very definite improvement but far too over priced for what you get. One last detail; it comes with its own remote control that is about the size of a credit card in ALL dimensions and tends to get lost very easily.

Would I recommend it to a friend, possibly. Is is worth the price, definitely not. Is it better than the stock sound that comes out of the LG, yes. So I rated it in the middle and leave it up to you to decide.

review_title: If you like your jerky tough, you may like it. If you like your jerky on the soft side, you'll hate it
review_text: Let me first say that for flavor, I give this 4 stars, maybe even 5.  It's got the smokiness of the ghost pepper with the slightly sweet taste of the habanero (not hanabero, like the typo in the item listing) and the flavor is blended quite well. It's very hot, but with purpose and the flavor really comes through. It's not just hot for the sake of being hot. I have a very high tolerance for heat and it definitely got me going.  For texture though, this jerky is a 2 star at best, maybe even 1 star. It is TOUGH! When I say tough, this jerky is like chewing on tree bark. I don't mind tough jerky in general, but I really hard a hard time with this. It wasn't so hard it was like a jaw breaker, but it's quite difficult to bite into and is a chore to eat. I got the 8oz so it's two 4oz packs. I haven't even touched the 2nd pack due to how difficult the 1st one was to chew. So to recap, 4-5 stars on flavor, 1-2 stars on texture, so a 3 star overall. BTW, a word of warning: It's very oily, and it seems like it's pretty much straight capsaicin oil, so use dish detergent to wash your hand thoroughly after, and don't touch any sensitive areas for a while.

product_name: SHARKK Aluminum Surge Protector 4 Port USB Outlet Extender Power Strip for Home Office Power Strips with 4 USB Smart Rapid Charger Charge Ports and 5 Foot Cord
review_title: Actually 4.5 stars.  Great idea with a few minor issues and suggestions.
review_text: I was asked by Sharkk to evaluate and review the Sharkk Power Strip and USB smart charger.  This power strip has four AC plugs and four smart USB charging ports in one device.  The power strip is 10  5/8"  long, 2 3/4 " high and 1 1/4" deep.  The cord is 5' long and is three pronged, just like the AC outlets.  The four outlets are spaced so that four 1 1/2 " transformers can fit with no issues.  Since the power strip also has four USB ports, it is designed to be mounted above a desk and not sitting on the floor.  With this in mind the design of the power strip is very smooth with the sides curved instead of square edges, a very European style that is very pleasing to the eye and makes this more than just a utilitarian object.  The power strip appears to be aluminum with plastic around the AC outlets and on the two end caps.  All in all a very stylish design.   The four USB ports are able to provide 6 amps total with a single port providing up to 2.4 amps, enough to charge an IPAD air with no problems.  It should be able to charge two IPADs at the same time.  This is one of the few  USB chargers that I have encountered that can actually charge a Nook HD.  Unfortunately, there is no capacity information printed on the power strip stating this information.  I got this from the web site.  The back of the power strip does state that the strip can handle 15 amps and for a capacity of 1675 watts and is only 120 volts.  The strip can be mounted on the wall and two screw holes are provided for that purpose.  It would be nice if they provided a paper drilling template to mount it but at least on this version. review_title: tastes great, had issues with dissolving, but resolved
review_text: I'm a longtime user of Trader Joe's stevia extract powder.  I got the BulkSupplements stevia extract powder to try for free and review.  Well, the flavor is fine, but it has difficulty dissolving.  The Trader Joe's stevia is called a powder, but the BulkSupplements stevia is more like dust or flour.  It's almost too fine, so it tends to clump when added to liquids, whether hot, cold, or room temp.  Since it is so super fine, it takes even less than the TJ's.  So, where two of the teeny weeny scoops of the TJ's would be just right, only one scoop of the BulkSupplements stevia was needed.  I first used the same amount, and it was too sweet.  I tried mixing half TJ's and half BulkSupplements stevia together before adding to liquid, and there was still clumping.  It did eventually dissolve, with lots of stirring.  I have found a similar effect with spices, such as onion powder or garlic powder.  They're called powders, but they're actually tiny little granules.  If they are actually powders, with a flour or dust-like fineness, they tend to clump and not dissolve well.  For the quantity and sweetening power, the BulkSupplements stevia extract powder is a great deal!  TJ's, or Now brand 100% stevia extract powder goes for about $10/oz.  I'm pleased to have been offered this product to try and review.  If I had purchased it, I might be more distressed at the way it dissolves.  I'll continue working with it, but I'm unsure if I'll purchase this in the future.  Some folks find an unpleasant aftertaste with stevia, and some don't.  I've only found an unpleasant aftertaste when using products that are not 100% pure stevia, that have other stuff added, like inulin or dextrose.  Stick with 100% pure stevia for best results.  Update: Jan. 2016  I got some erythritol to mix with this stevia powder, and it's worked out great.  I mix two tablespoons of erythritol (Swerve brand) and one tablespoon plus two teaspoons of the Bulk Supplements stevia powder.  It's just the right sweetness, dissolves well, and, I think, works out pretty good cost-wise.  I'm now getting low on the stevia powder, but have quite a bit of the erythritol left.  (Erythritol by itself tastes weird, and gives a strange cooling sensation/mouth-feel.)  I will probably re-order this stevia powder.  Update 2-4-16.   I ordered more of this stevia, planning on mixing it with erythritol again, but I don't need to.  This batch is dissolving much more readily than the one I got previously.  Yay!  Tastes great.  Also, this package has info I don't recall being on the previous batch. (Maybe it was there and I didn't see it.)  It says:  stevia extract....40mg.    steviol glycosides...38 mg (per 40 mg serving).  Rebaudiosides...22mg (per 40 mg serving). On their website it shows Stevia extract...40mg.    Steviol glycosides 90% 38mg.   Steviosides...35mg.    Rebaudiosides...16mg

All in all, I like the unit, and would recommend it.

I gave four stars instead of 5 since the flavor isn't that strong, but honestly what makes the other drinks more flavorful is all the added crap that is horrible for you in them, so... It's a trade off. I would recommend trying one in the store first before buying a 12 pack. That's what I did and thought it was worth buying more of as my go-to caffeine source. I'll be buying more in the future.

review_title: Know longer awesome and dropping score to 1 star.
review_text:
UPDATE: 9/13/2015
Both pairs purchased are now worthless. One of the ear pieces spins on the black hard coiled plastic (see product photo) that reaches around the head. This causes the ear piece not to sit right on ear and is uncomfortable. Both now lose power quickly because the battery seems to short circuit due to sweat entering the ear encasement. When it happens, all you can hear is a quick whistle and then nothing. Once it dries out, it will only power up after a recharge...even then, the play time is diminished each time it happens. My wife is buying me another brand for my birthday.

RECOMMENDATIONS TO MANUFACTURER:
-Better seal around black hard wire connecting to ear pieces and all other places where moisture can enter the device. Sweat from an average workout shouldn't cause this much of an issue.
-Better anchor for ear piece attached to the black hard wire to keep from breaking then spinning around loosely.

UPDATE: 7/31/2015
I purchased a pair of these headphones in May of 2015. That pair seem to be still working...mainly because I gave them to my wife who liked them, but hasn't been able to use them much while running because of other issues. The pair I bought in June, that I use at least 4 days a week have "crapped" out on me 3 times already in the middle of workouts. They just completely lose power even though they have been recently recharged. They will work again once I plug them back in for a short recharge. Quite annoying and nothing I hate worse than being stopped during an intense workout. I need the music to pace me along with the voice timer that I listen to when time to change exercises. If it's the sweat that is causing the problem, then this set is obviously the wrong equipment for exercising. Granted they are awesome because they don't interfere with exercising, nor do they fall off, but I cannot deal with faulty headphones...so de-motivating!
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Original Review:
I have now had these headphones for a week solid and have put them through my daily workouts and I have to say...awesome!!! There are a few quirks, but nothing I haven't been able to handle at this point.

Pros:
- COMPACT!!! They fit nicely in the case in which comes with the product. Since I have a gym bag, there's no chance of them getting lost or tangled up in the bag with my other gear like regular wired headphone would have.
- They don't fall off my head...and I have a BIG head! I used to have an LG Tone Bluetooth headset that worked fine, but as soon as I started to do my abdominal workout or used a decline bench, they would slide off my neck. The only thing keeping them from hitting the ground was the ear buds stuck in my ears. *smh*
-Easy to use and no loose parts.
-Charge fairly fast and have a pretty good charge on them. I went almost a week without charging them and I used them a few hours each day.
-Not noise cancelling! Which is good when you're in public running or walking the dog...you can still hear enough around you that you don't need to have one of the ear pieces slightly off the ear. With my LG Tones, I would would always take one bud out of my ears so I could hear around me. ie...Other runners coming from behind, cars, animals, etc.
-Sound is not Bose quality, but still pretty good. I can enjoy my workouts with good sounding, CLEAR tunes without the wires and mess that wired headphones bring.
-Sturdy and solid.

CONS:
-Bass is a bit weak. I had to use the EQ in my phone for the 1st time ever to turn up the bass a bit. Other than that, no complaints on the sound quality.
-In one week, I have lost connection to my phone in the middle of an intense workout. VERY frustrating to have to stop and get the headphones and phone paired back up. I suspect that this was isolated, but we will see...I will update review if further issues arise.
-They need to add a voice for battery levels. IE...When turning on head phones, Say "Power on, battery level High"...or medium..or low. Just nice to have to the warnings.
-My wife tried on the headphones and she has a much smaller head and lots of hair. Headphones were not so cooperative staying on her head. We could have played with them more to get them to stay, but her patience was low that day.

I will update more if issue arise...but I do have to say that out of 10 plus different headphones that I have paid lots of money for, these are by far the best.for battery levels. product_name: CTYRZCH(TM) Wireless VGA Signal Extender Booster Signal Ethernet Cable Including a Wireless Transmitter and a Receiver 1080P Extending the VGA Signal 60 Meters by a CAT-5e/6 Cable
review_title: Confusing product descriptions detract from a product that actually works as designed for the intended purpose.
review_text:
First of all, I think this product does exactly what it is intended to do. However, the Amazon site documentation, and the product packaging have, at best ambiguous and, at worst misleading, information. What I really wanted was something to transmit and receive a VGA signal through the internet. The Amazon description includes the following:

"The transmitter which is linked with main engine will convert the VGA signal to standard TCP/IP and transmit by internet.
This receiver which is connected with the display will convert the standard TCP/IP signal into VGA signal."

At another place it says the transmission is over a single wire. To me those statements are contradictory. I expected the latter was correct, and that the former has a very limited definition of "internet". I don't think just using a Cat5e or Cat6 cable really defines an internet transmission.

I ordered it, since it was inexpensive, to be sure.The good news is that if you make the connection across a single ethernet cable, it works flawlessly. Across an actual internet connection (even a wired one) it does nothing.

To further confuse things, the front of the box it comes in describes what it actually does, but there is another statement there that I can't understand at all. It says:

"Converts Coaxial or Toslink digital audio signals to analog L/R audio"

That would be a neat trick since it has no Toslink, Coaxial or analog audio connectors. This text is directly beside a picture of the product that clearly shows that statement is impossible. So what the heck is that about? It didn't matter to me because I wasn't looking for that functionality, but it certainly is bizarre. So if you need to extend a VGA signal over a longer Cat5e or Cat6 cable, you're in business, but don't expect anything else.

product_name: Bicycle Dragon Back Playing Cards (Pack of 3), Blue/Red/Gold
review_title: A good deal on three very colorful decks.
review_text:
More great quality cards from USPCC. I've been looking at these for a while, and finally picked up this set. All three decks have the same high quality card stock. Other than the colors, these are the same, except for the original gold design.

The gold deck doesn't actually have any metallic inks present; the dragons are two tones of brown or tan. The deck has a color 808 Joker, and a black-only guarantee Joker. The royals use the darker tan from the dragon art, with a dark blue and a dark red. That same dark red - or burgundy - is the only red used on these decks, so the two red suits are the same darker color. The Joker uses these same colors as well.

The red deck has five colors present in its backs, though these are all fairly dark, so it doesn't see like it's that colorful. The same jokers are present as in the gold deck, though the colors are different; he's decked out entirely in dark red with tan trim, and the bike is colored a dark green-blue. On the faces here, the colors are the same dark burgundy red and green-blue colors, with light tan trim. The red suits use the same dark red.

The blue deck also uses five colors for the backs, with the dragons comprised of two shades of blue, and the trim using two shades of tan. The Joker is decked out in blue this time, with a dark tan bike and light tan trim. As expected, the face cards use these same colors. However, the red suits here are actually blue; blue diamonds and blue hearts.

The red and blue decks come with one double-backed card each, as well as an ad card. The gold deck doesn't have any extraneous cards whatsoever. The red and blue decks are also very subtle one-way backs.

Definitely well worth the money. Ideal for collectors and players alike. If you like these designs, there are also yellow and green dragon back designs available.

I had a Summer infant one I liked better that felt like better quality.
