product_name: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen 1287632 Beolit 15
review_text:
Many people have long had a need for a portable sound system that can move from office to workout room to patio. Once upon a time, this role was filled by ungainly "blasters". The advent of Bluetooth has enabled a flood of new devices, and Bang & Olufsen have joined the fray with rather mixed results.

Out of the box, the Beolit 15 makes a good first impression. While fairly small, it's solid with some heft. The look is tasteful and conservative (we'll talk about the strap in a little while). I appreciated the fact that there's an internal power supply--no wall wart--and that the power cable tucks nicely into the back. Bluetooth pairing with my iPhone was quick, and music was coming out ten minutes after taking it out of the box. At first I enjoyed the wide frequency range, but the thumping bass soon got the better of me. Bass is usually the attention-grabber in a sound system, but too much of it can wear out its welcome quickly. That was the case here.

So it was time to look at the user guide. It turns out that the booklets included with the Beolit were mainly warnings and warrantees. The user guide itself was only a couple of pages. No specifications were included and the instructions were at the reading level of a cat. How to tame that bass? I found the web page for the product line. There was really only a page of specs there: most of the website was dedicated to the designer and the overall look was more like a lifestyle catalog. But that's what B&O has always been.

It turns out that there are no tone controls of any sort on the device. At a minimum, some sort of "superbass" switch would have been appreciated. in the end, an EQ app from the App Store was able to smooth the sound and achieve a satisfactory balance. At a minimum, B&O should have provided such an app with the device.

There are more positive things to say. Bluetooth range was quite good, with solid connection all around a large house--even across two floors. Battery life was claimed at 12 hours and that was easily exceeded at moderate playing levels. Higher sound levels would probably shorten battery life somewhat, but I think this claim was easily met.

But there were many missed opportunities. There's a USB connector, but it's charge-only. If you want to connect your iPod and charge while you're playing, you'll need two cables--audio AND USB. Even the base audio system in my car will play music through the USB cable. B&O missed the boat on this. There are also no play controls other than volume buttons. There are no start/stop or skip buttons. This means that you always have to keep your phone or tablet close by. There's more than enough room for 2 or 3 more buttons. Not having those buttons really impairs the ease-of-use of this device.

B&O also proudly proclaims "240 watts peak power". Peak power is a sham term that respectable manufacturers dropped decades ago. Obviously some marketing type at B&O likes big numbers but doesn't know what they mean. If you dig a little you'll find that the Beolit has a pair of 35-watt amps. That's really quite a respectable number for a device like this and it's more than adequate for the task. Why not use the real number. It's worth noting that they distribute amps and speakers in such a way that the result is mono. This was done to ensure even frequency distribution around the room (not fully effective, but fair), but I'd have preferred stereo. Of course if you're playing music for a cookout, you don't really care.

And there's that strap. It's a piece of unfinished leather, attached to a couple of pegs--just like a guitar strap. It clashes with the overall styling and gives the Beolit the appearance of a lunch pail. The unit does need some way be carried, so why not a handle? There's plenty of room and it could be nicely-styled. The strap looks like an afterthought.

Bang & Olufsen hasbeen around for quite a while, known more for their styling (from beautiful to bizarre) than their audio quality (middle of the pack). It's clear they have the makings of a very nice product line here, but they need a strong UX (user experience) advocate inside the company. That would make an enormous difference.

product_name: Secret Outlast Clear Gel Antiperspirant and Deodorant Scent, 2.7 Ounce
review_title: It's here! It's clear! It's not that special!
review_text:
I received a free sample of this product from Secret in order to test it out, so for a few weeks I used my normal deodorant on one armpit, and the Outlast Clear Gel on the other to get a good comparison. Final conclusion: It's just ok. Not bad, but not the greatest thing ever to happen to my armpits.

I generally don't like gel deodorants...something about putting a gooey liquid in my armpit is less than appealing. As gels go though, this does dry relatively quickly and is only a little sticky. The product is clear and leaves no white marks, but I've never had any problems with white marks myself, and definitely not any issues with clumping (eew!). If white marks are a concern for you, this may be a product worth trying out.

The odor protection continues to be inconsistent, but so does my current deodorant. The most significant thing for me was the scent of the product. The other versions of Secret Clear Gel have a very clear label indicating the scent. The fact that the Completely Clean version doesn't mention scent at all is somewhat misleading, and I assumed that it would be relatively unscented. If you don't want a noticeable smell coming from your armpits throughout the day, be sure to get the version that says "unscented", not Completely Clean. All in all, Secret Outlast doesn't seem to be any better than my usual brand, but it's not any worse either. It may be worth a shot if you have issues with white marks!

I would recommend this product to anyone looking for a good quality video monitor.

review_text:
Just received my tea today! It arrived in a small tin with the tea and a bag clip. There are two clear round sticker things that hold the tin lid for shipping so you need to remove those first. I cut the bag open with scissors and inside you find the dried flowers.

I did not see any instructions so I decided to try 4 flowers to 8 ounces at first. I find this makes a nicely mild tea that does not require any sweeter. It is really mild made this way. When I went to make a second cup I noticed there are English instructions on the bottom of the tin!! lol Says to stop in a shady, dry place (no strong orders in air) and to brew with 5-10 bugs in 250ml (1 cup) of warm water for 3 minutes.

So I did that next but did not wait 3 minutes because I do not like strong tea. I brewed it about 1.5 minutes. Very tasty!!! I used my French Press to brew the tea since I do not have an infuser. Works great!

The description of the Chrysanthemum tea is "bitter sweet" . Brewed mildly I personally do not really get a bitter flavor. I did let it seep longer and as it sits, to me the flavor becomes strong and then it is bitter to me.

Overall I really like this tea and am sipping on it as I write this post. I think this is going to become a favorite for me.

I did receive this tea at a discount for the purpose of testing and was asked to write an unbiased review when I was done testing. All of my reviews are uninfluenced by the vendors as I just enjoy helping out shoppers.

review_text:
After reading tons of great reviews for the Britax (no matter what type of Britax seat) I decided it was a clear choice. Nope! I own two marathons, one for my 3 year old and one for my 22 month old. Both seats have repeatedly had issues with the strap fraying near the base of the seat. It frays to the point where the strap is nearly severed. I've contacted Britax and they did send me new straps, but it continues to happen so it's clearly a manufacturing flaw....a very unsafe flaw. I also have an issue with how difficult it is to tighten or loosen the straps. They barely move, which might be why they are fraying. Lastly, the straps are continuously tangled and twisted. Just terrible!

We have 2 Recarro seats in my husbands car and much prefer those. The straps slide easily, never fray, and have a white stripe on the outside so even if they do twist it's very easy to see which way to turn them to un-twist them. Even though my son won't need this type of seat for much longer, I'm tempted to trash the Britax and get a new Recarro since at least i'll know he'll be safe.

product_name: JLab Epic Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Sports Earbuds with 10 Hour Battery and IPX4 Waterproof Rating, Black
review_text:
I've been using mine for only a few hours now, so this is just a first impression.

Comfort is good. It took me quite some time to ajust it properly(both wire and ear piece), but once you find a good position it fits nicely.

Sound quality is pretty good too. I think there is a bit too much bass and it ends up overshadowing the treble, but an EQ easily solves that.

The bluetooth connectivity however has been really bad so far. The range itself seems to be fine, but the connection is too unstable. Sometimes, just by putting my phone inside my pocket or maybe covering the earbuds' volume control with my hands, the music starts breaking up badly. And sometimes it keeps working perfectly well even with some distance and heavy/dense objects between the earbuds and my phone. There doesn't seem to be a pattern, and it's driving me mad.

My phone is a Nexus 5 and I've extensively used its bluetooth connection with other audio devices before and I've never had this kind of issue.

Overall these are really good earbuds but this bluetooth problem is just too annoying.

EDIT: I did some tests and the connectivity is not unstable, it is permanently terrible. Way worse than I had previously thought. Even the slightest interferance (eg: my hands or my empty backpack, or even just tilting my head a little bit) can completely block out the bluetooth signal, which is absurd for a $100 device.

review_text: Very pleased with these speakers.  They are an excellent value proposition.  I bought them straight from music direct and I have them paired with a NAD D3020, which I also got at MD. Since I'm not an audio reviewer it's difficult for me to articulate why I like these speakers so much, and I don't just want to regurgitate a bunch of stuff I've read in speaker reviews.  With that said, these speakers are pretty tonally neutral.  Highs are pleasant, not harsh at all.  The midrange is also very pleasing to my ears.  Low end is very satisfactory to me, but I'm sure others would want to pair this with a sub.  I've noticed that these speakers have no trouble resolving recordings with lots of bass  In fact, like all good speakers, these sound best with good records, but they are more than fair to lesser quality records.  One cool thing about the 220's is that they have a downward firing bass port and this means they can be placed pretty close to a wall, which helps bass response.  Vocal clarity is the one thing that really jumps out at me with these speakers.  The vocals are crisp and right in the middle of the soundstage.  TV dialogue also has the same vocal clarity.  Overall a great set of speakers.

product_name: Aspen Pet Lebistro Programmable Food Dispenser
review_title: A few niceties, but overall poor execution
review_text: While this automatic pet feeder certainly accomplishes its main goal of automatically feeding your pet a measured amount of food up to 3 times per day, I believe it has some major design flaws that make it not worth purchasing. I'll start with the good features and then list the bad.  Good: 1. You can program the machine to dispense food for up to 3 times per day (nicely labeled as Breakfast, Lunch, or Dinner). 2. You can program each of these times to dispense food in intervals of 1/4 cup. Meaning, each of the 3 times that food may be dispensed can have different amounts of food dispensed and in intervals of 1/4 cup (e.g. 1/4 cup for breakfast, 1/4 for lunch and 1/2 for dinner). 3. The container can hold a relatively large amount of food. I don't know the exact volume but I have to refill it roughly once every 3 weeks and I feed my cat 1/2 cup of food per day. 4. It's relatively easy to take it apart, clean each separate piece, and then reconstruct it.  So far so good. Here are the bad points: 1. Perhaps the biggest design flaw is that my cat can hack the machine to give her extra food. She figured out that she can reach her paw up the chute where the food falls and push the hatch to allow extra food to fall. The way the machine is designed is that it has a wheel with four extruding flaps, and 1/4 cup of food can fit between each flap for a total of 1 cup in the wheel. My cat can push the flap to drop down an extra 1/4 cup of food. This means that when it's time to feed her, the wheel rotates and no food drops down so I don't know if the machine actually turned the wheel or if my cat pushed the flap to get her meal early. 2. The bowl from which your pet eats, and into which the food falls from the chute, is poorly designed. It does not click into place when you connect it to the machine, and it often falls off at the slightest touch. Because it is loose, food often falls around the bowl and makes a mess. The plus side is that it is easy to clean, but that should have been a given anyways. 3. The controls are very non-intuitive and require me to reference the manual every time I use them. There are three buttons, Enter, Down, and Up, and their usages are confusing and difficult, if not impossible, to remember. 4. Continuing with the poor control design, if you want to manually dispense food, you have to hold the up button for 3 seconds and 1/4 cup of food will come out. If you keep holding the button then it will keep dispensing food indefinitely until you hold it again. This happens to me roughly 1/2 the time, which is quite a lot because I manually feed my cat sometimes due to not being able to tell if she's gotten food per the #1 bad point above. 5. It does not have AC power. It seems to last a very long time on batteries, but not being able to plug it in and not worry about it is pretty annoying. Edit: 6. As another downside to the bowl being detachable -- my cat has figured out how to pull it out of the feeder...so that when she does this (and I don't notice), her food gets dispensed all over the floor. This is extremely annoying, and a further indication of the lack of thought put into the fundamental design of this product.  I hope this review helps you in your purchase.

product_name: Bluetooth Speaker, DKnight Magicbox Ultra-Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker Powerful Sound with build in Microphone, Works for Cellphone
review_text: When I first got this, I really liked it. It was annoying to not have volume buttons on the speaker, but I dealt with it. It was also annoying that if I was playing music from my phone and received a call, the ring and voice would come through the speaker and I had to manually move it back to my phone. But I dealt with it because I enjoyed playing music through the speaker. However, I have only had it for 3 months and am already having troubles. My phone is having trouble connecting to it and then the speaker will drop the bluetooth connection - sometimes mid-song. When I play music, my phone will say it's playing on the speaker but the speaker isn't playing the music. I have to drop the connection and re-connect it to get music to play. I got so sick of the connection issues I bought the Anker Portable Speaker (A7909) and WOW - the Anker is totally better. The sound quality is so much better and battery life is twice as long. I didn't realize the DKnight sound quality was poor until I played it side-by-side with the Anker. Voices are crisper, bass is richer and I hear the various parts of the song better. It also has volume buttons on the speaker and if I get a call, the persons voice doesn't transfer to the speaker. I wish I had just paid more a few months ago and saved myself the hassle. I realize this has turned into a review of the Anker but I hate reading poor reviews of a product and wonder what product ended up working for that person... so if you can spare a few more dollars, buy the Anker ($27 vs $70). If you are strapped on cash, the DKnight will do and hopefully yours lasts longer than 3 months with no issues.

product_name: Sony NWZE38 Walkman MP3 Player
review_title: Not as good as older Walkman
review_text: I bought this player about a year ago. I intended to use it to replace an older 8-gig Sony Walkman. The sound quality seems about the same as the older Walkman, but in almost all ways the older Walkman is better than this one. So I've kept my older one for use in situations where the new one is frustrating (when driving, walking or exercising at the gym).  My biggest frustration is just turning the thing on. To turn it on, you press any of the buttons. Then you wait a few seconds until it says it's on hold. Then you hold down the OPTION button for a couple of seconds until that goes away. Then it goes into a "creating library" phase that usually lasts from 2 to 20 seconds. Then you press the play/pause button and it finally starts to play. Figure around 8-20 seconds to turn it on, while having to watch the screen. So I especially do not recommend this player if you, like me, want to use the player in the accessory input of your car radio. It's just too much of a driving distraction to turn it on. For the older Walkman, a touch of a button turns it on. If it's been used within the last 24 hours, it comes on immediately. Otherwise a several second delay but no other actions needed.  The older Walkman isn't much larger than this one, but it has a much larger screen. It displays more info about the song being displayed - title, performer, album, year released and music category. This one only alternates between showing the performer and song title.  The layout of the older Walkman made it very easy to use the controls by feel. When in my car, going for a walk, exercising in the gym or listening to music in bed, I like to be able to control it by feel. With the layout this one has, I have a much more difficult time using them by feel, and often hit the wrong button. Of course, it is a lot better than a touch screen if you want to go by feel, but Sony has really gone backwards from the older model.  The one feature that this one has that my older one did not haveis a sleep timer. I really like that feature, except that it's implemented poorly in this device. When the sleep timer is active, you cannot use either the BACK button or the OPTION button without first cancelling the sleep timer. This means you can't, among other things: Switch to a different playlist. Search for an album or artist. Display details about the song being played. You can't even display the current time.  Playlists are similar on both devices, with one big difference. The older Walkman remembers the songs you've played in a playlist, while the newer one doesn't. The newer one doesn't do this. So, for example, if I have a 200-title playlist and listen to it over ten sessions of 20 songs per session, turning the device off in the meantime, the older Walkman will have played each song exactly once. The newer one will have played a lot of duplicates, and a lot of songs wouldn't have been heard. In practice, I usually listen to about 10 songs each evening, and I usually hear at least two or three songs that I listened to the night before.   So - sound quality is fine, it's only the controls that are frustrating. I use Windows Media Player to construct playlists, and use the automatic sync to keep the two players in sync - works great with both players, so no gripes there.

But if you use your other hand as a wall and somewhat press your hair against the brush it CAN detangle small tangles. product_name: Natural Dog Company Travel PawTection .15oz
review_title: Worst Organic Lip Balm Ever...Oh wait, it's paw protectant.
review_text:
First off, I got burned on this purchase, but it was by my own doing. I should have read closer and looked at the product specs with more scrutiny.

Second, this product would probably work if you have one of those super tiny dogs that doesn't normally walk around outside in the back yard or go for walks. The product is smaller than some of the lip balms I've ordered, and comes in the same size tube. For $7.95 I was expecting more than organic lip balm. <---Oddly enough, it contains many of the same ingredients as organic lip balm products I've purchased in the past. So I might as well have put $4.95 organic lip balm on my dogs feet and saved $3.

There isn't sufficient product to last the entire outdoor season and cover the feet of a small (14lbs, so not tiny, but not big) chihuahua mix....Much less the feet of a 70lb Lab mix. I put this stuff on his feet and immediately used 1/3 of it. The product does not absorb nor glide on smoothly. If the intention were to not heal/soothe/absorb, but to provide a wax barrier, I would expect a smooth application that leaves a thick waxy layer on the dogs foot. Instead I had bumps and plops of product in some places, and none on other parts of the paw pad.

I appreciate the natural ingredients, but here's the thing: It turns out MOST PAW PROTECTOR products already use natural ingredients as dogs are prone to licking off the product or using their paws to scratch their face/eyes. So I find it a bit deceptive toward pet owners who want to look into protecting their pets feet, but don't know enough....

product_name: Woodees Vintage Noise Isolating Earphones with 3 Button Microphone
review_title: Great sound but build quality is down a little
review_text:
Like other customers, I had trouble with the paint finish being chipped on it from the factory on this set that was purchased through Amazon. I called SAS and asked about it (the only way to contact them. The email route doesn't work or gets ignored). They RMA'd them with little trouble and I received a new set promptly. The new set looked and sounded great when I used it for the first month with my iPhone 4S. The main problem I had with them is that when using them to make a hands-free call, the person on the other end would hear themselves in a severe echo. I couldn't hear any sound problems at all during the call. If I unplugged the earbuds the echo would go away until I connected them again. I tried using a set of the Apple Earpods with the same phone and there isn't any echo problem with them at all so I believe the echo is from the Woodees earbuds. The Mic/ Volume controls on the earbuds finally died abruptly one day but the sound is still good like always. It doesn't have a damaged cable or anything like would normally cause something like that to go out. I believe the Mic/ Volume control had a electrical defect that caused it to go bad. Since I had another problem with this set I tried to email them again from the same email regarding the paint and have not received any response over a two week period. I will have to call but haven't had the time.

Only other gripe is the earbud tips are sized weird for my ear canal. The largest one seems to be too big (but it fits the best out of the three sizes) and the medium size seems to be too small where they don't seal properly. I also had to get them angled just right to get a good seal even with the large size, otherwise the sound quality is poor. I would suggest a set of the Comply earbud tips made for these earbuds. I haven't tried them out yet since the Mic part quit working before I had a chance to buy them so I quit using the set until I get it replaced.

TL;DR - Product looks and sounds great, build quality is questionable and customer service is lacking since the only way you can get a response is to call. The email doesn't work apparently.

review_title: good taste and decent texture for a GF item
review_text:
These are a little hard compared to wheat crackers, but for a gluten free product, the texture is not bad. These are pretty thin and they taste really salty. So it is amazing to me that one serving only has 135 mg of sodium. That's much lower than I expected based on taste (which is a good thing).

I like how a lot of the grains in these are whole grains (i.e., brown rice flour, whole grain yellow corn) instead of just simple starches. In my experience, starchy (and non-whole-grain) GF products are easier to come by than versions with some whole grains. These are fairly low in fat and have a little fiber and protein. You can see the full ingredients list and nutrition facts panel in the product images.

Because these are pretty salty, you would want to use savory spreads or dips if you are going that direction. (And don't use anything that will conflict with the flavor of sesame seeds, because that is definitely noticeable here.) Cheese and hummus would both be good. These are also vegetarian. And they don't stick in or on your teeth after eating, unlike some other crackers I've had lately!

Overall, I love the flavor and the texture is something I can live with. Even though I don't need to eat GF, I would seriously consider buying these again.

review_title: Very pleased with this pillow! Comfortable while still promoting good meditation posture!
review_text:
Alright, I'm an avid meditator (minimum of once daily, prefer twice a day) so I'm no stranger to meditation pillows. The problem with a lot of meditation pillows is that they are under stuffed or just too darn soft. Part of meditation is having good posture and if its too squishy its harder to maintain your posture. Another big issue is that they tend to be heavy and cumbersome.

This pillow is good on both fronts. Its very light for a meditation pillow and its stuffed to the gills. Before buying, I read a bunch of the reviews and I noticed all the negative ones mentioned that its "too hard" and I can only assume that the people who wrote that are new to meditation. This pillow is way more comfortable than many others I have used while still being sturdy enough to promote correct posture. I personally do mindfulness (Vipassana) meditation and part of that is not allowing yourself to be too comfortable because that will lull you to sleep or make you forget your mission.

This pillow is perfect for my needs and I believe anyone else who is in need of a meditation pillow would do well to buy this one. The price is pretty good and the quality (of mine at least) is fantastic.

I was lucky enough to snag a discount in exchange for testing and reviewing this meditation pillow. Having said that, I wouldn't hesitate to pay full price for it and I have already recommended it to two of my friends that also do daily meditation.

review_text:
I received this item in exchange for my honest opinion. I wasn't able to install it for awhile due to a family emergency but now that I'm back in town and find myself home without my hunky boy to install it for me I realized just how much it's great to have him around ;)

Pros:
-It's packaged well and the box explains what's inside so it's easy to keep spare parts and such stowed away and easy to find
-It's easy to understand the workings of it once you remove it from the box.
-It's defiantly sturdy and can hold my monitor with no problems at all
-The slim design is much better for space saving minimalism than most. If you want to have the option to swing your monitor out or move it around on a daily bases this is not for you.

Cons:
-Installing it alone was a bit of a challenge but again, I usually depend on my man to do that for me so it's my own issue
-I was a bit confused on exactly how I was going to mount my monitor at the angle I'm used to having it since it was going to be on the wall and the slim design doesn't leave much room for error in initial mounting without having to remove it and start over. It's very hard to move it once it's in place so instead of struggling with that everyday I just placed it where I needed it to be and re mounted the monitor at that angle.
-The instructions could have been a bit clearer on how to install through studs without anchors.
-The hardware included seemed to be for a larger TV mount than I was looking for so I just used some bolts and washers we had. This mount is made to support TV's that are much heavier than the 24" computer monitor I was mounting above my desk so I didn't feel that I needed screws over 2 inches long. I didn't use the anchors since I firmly believe you should always mount electronics to the studs or a board and then into studs. I'm sure the hardware is built very well and will work for much heavier items just fine.

Overall this is a great product and I'd highly recommend it for home or office wall mount computer monitor use. It doesn't claim to be something it's not and what it does claim to do- it does well! product_name: Comfort Zone Feliway Diffuser Kit for Cat Calming
review_title: It probably works, but I don't think it's a miracle
review_text:
I bought these because I was going on a week's vacation being cared for a pet sitter during this time and they have never been left alone overnight before. I was sure this would have been a stressful event for them; but maybe it was more so for me. I don't know if these worked while I was gone or could tell once I got back.

I plugged them in 3 days before we left for our trip as they recommend for full effectiveness they need to work for 7 days. I plugged one upstairs in bedroom in the middle of the house with the door open to the hall and one downstairs behind a chair they love to scratch to my displeasure.

The only thing I did notice when I got back is that one of my cats suddenly liked hanging out in the hallway by that bedroom whenever she was relaxing or suddenly became stressed (loud noise, etc.). But as far as the one downstairs, I don't think that stopped them from wanting to scratch the chair even thought there is literally a giant cat tree with several scratching posts next to it. I did notice that while we were away they liked sleeping on the couch because I had to vacuum a thick layer of cat hair that was in the shape of a sleeping cat.

Relatives and neighbors stopped by to check on the cats and both said they seemed calm. My neighbor brought over her 8 month old baby and both cats were friendly; they were scared of her as a newborn.

I will have to test this product again to see how effective it is. My cats without a diffuser are generally sweet, laid-back, and happy go lucky.

review_title: Ports stop working randomly! Power reset fixes that.
review_text:
This is our team charger at the office, the ports unfortunately sometimes stop working randomly, I was thinking it was a faulty port at the beginning, as only one had the issue, and I was assuming that, well, one out of six is still a keeper. But then I unplugged it and plugged it again, and all ports were working!

Then, a couple of hours later, bam, two ports stop working... Always a cord unplugging will reset the issue, but it is annoying. Sometimes four ports don't work, then two, and so on...

I think the PowerIQ circuitry isn't working properly or wasn't tested enough. As there is a higher probability that a port that hasn't been used in a while will not work when a cable is connected. So, maybe there is a shutdown in the circuitry that doesn't turn on again.

But well, now everybody at the office knows that a quick unplug/plug will reset the charger, so, we are keeping it.

product_name: IRIS Exercise Panel Pet Playpen with Door - 34 Inch
review_title: Surprisingly high quality for a plastic product
review_text:
This product is of surprisingly high quality. I put together dozens of plastic things of similar complexity as the kids were growing up, and expected this to be the same barely-fitting-together, loosely assembled, rickety thing. But no - the parts fit together snugly and cleanly, the few metal parts fit in their designated spots perfectly, and the whole thing feels solid. Another nice touch - the sizes of the screw-on metal parts are selected such that they won't fit in another part's place, so you can basically do what little assembly is required without looking at the instructions - again, an unexpected level of sophistication. I was planning to glue on some no-slip rubber pads on the bottom to prevent the whole thing sliding too easily on the hardwood floor, but no - non-slip rubber feet are already included. That last bit of touching forethought almost made me cry.

One little gripe I have about this enclosure is that I wish it would fold up like an accordion when you want to put it away. As it is, the joined sections fold neatly in one direction but not in the other. So to put it away, I will have to separate it into four two-part sections rather than simply break the circle and fold up the whole thing as one piece. I imagine there is a good reason to not allow the sections to fold both ways that I have yet to discover, otherwise it would be done - the rest of the product is too well thought for this to be omitted unintentionally.

review_title: I feel like I just lit $28 of fire after buying these things :(
review_text:
I found these sticks on amazon because I was looking for a large quantity of bully sticks than I normally purchase. And after reading all the 5 star and the 1 star review - I naturally assumed that the other person that left a 1 star review for these stick was just angry person that didn't know what the hell they were talking about. So I ordered these sticks and anxiously waited for them to arrive so that my Italian greyhound could chew to his hearts content. When the sticks finally arrived, I noticed a few things about them that I just chose to ignore, but now after having them for 2 weeks, I'm just infuriated with myself for wasting $28. I REALLY REALLY REALLY tried to love these things. This brand had so many 5 start reviews - I thought there is no way I could go wrong with these things. Oh how stupid I was.....

PROS:
- You get LOT of bully sticks for your money. More than you get with almost any other bully stick brand sold on amazon. I can attest to this, since I have tried most of the brands currently sold on this site.

CONS:
- Brittle. The reason why you get so many bully sticks from this brand is because these sticks are thin/brittle. My 12 lbs, 9 month old Italian greyhound literally tore through 1 whole stick in less than an hour, which is absurd.
- Messy. Because these bully sticks are so brittle, as soon as my dog started chewing one, there was a trail of crunchy-fried remnants left all over my house.
- The smell. For someone who has never purchased high quality bully sticks, or someone is used to bully sticks that even have a slight pungent odor to them, you might get these and think, "ah, the smell isn't so bad", but that's where you are dead wrong. HIGH QUALITY BULLY STICKS DO NOT HAVE A NOTICABLE SMELL, AT ALL, PERIOD, END OF SENTENCE. And the fact that these bully sticks have a noticeable smell even before they have been chewed on by your dog should be the biggest red flag in the world...because once your dog starts chewing on this thing, the smell is intensified. I like to compare it to talking with someone who has mildly bad breathe. Their breath will not kill you, nor will it make you throw up, but damn - why should you have to stand there and be assaulted by that?
- Laughable quality control. Even in the 5 star reviews, and in the pictures posted for this product you will see that with this bag of sticks, you get some that are small and some that are large. But the worst part is that there seems to be little to no quality control because the sticks look like they have been deep fried in chicken grease.

I'm sure that this company is well intentioned, and I'm sure that the other 5 star reviewers feel justified in praising these sticks - most likely because they haven't actually tried a really high quality bully stick. product_name: Sony Dynamic closed-type headphones MDR-ZX310-H Lime Green/Gray
review_text:
I started taking an interest in headphones ever since my Dad brought me the sony mdr zx 100 for my birthday. At that age I didn't really care about sound quality or the cheapness of a headphone, just something I can listen to. But a couple of years forward my interest in headphones began to peak. I was listening from headphones like Audiotechnica m50x, JVC S500's and even the Sennheiser Momentums. So when I browsed amazon one day and found this little upgraded version of my first headphone, I was a bit excited. I started having this interest in comparing the two headphones. I also had brought the SONY MDR ZX 110 for a little extra.

So is it really an upgrade? Unfortunately, the looks and comfort of the headphone can only defined as an "upgrade".

The sound of the headphones is a bit bland, as it losses a little of the bass that the previous SONY MDR ZX 100 and 110 had. And though this headphone, the SONY MDR ZX310, has a bit, and I mean a tiny bit, more clarity then the SONY MDR ZX 100, it losses it's exciting signature from the previous models. And yes I have burned these headphones in for a decent amount of time.

In terms of outward appearance, these are definitely a step up. Personally the white and the lime green version of the headphone are a deal breaker for me as they really stand out. The only problem with the white is that it's literally a cheap looking version of the white SONY MDR ZX 600. On this headphone the outer rim of it gives off this nice black metallic look, similar to the SONY XB 450. There is also the green cord that comes with it, ending the tip of the L- shaped audio jack with a gray finish.

Yes this is a gray headphone, with green earpads, not black.

Comfort though is a bit debatable. You see these headphones come with ear pads that are like the cheap version of the SONY MDR ZX 600's. The feeling is like the same plastic material of the original SONY MDR ZX 100 but stretched out and more "clean" looking. There really isn't much padding as it's very thin, but because of the lightweight, you really wouldn't worry about it. They block out more sound outside then the SONY MDR ZX 100 and 110, but it's nowhere near the XB 450.

Also the pads do make your ear's sweat a little after extended use, but honestly I would pair them up with the replacement ear pads they sell on amazon for an extra five bucks. That's just my personal preference.

So if your excited about the sound these headphones deliver, you'll be a bit dissapointed, as the recessed bass is the only significant difference between the older models. But if your looking for a headphone your not afraid to wear in public, this is definitely a good start.d more "clean" looking. review_text:
I really like the concept and design of this speaker. While I will not be using it in any capacity where it will need to float, I am enjoying the security of having a waterproof speaker.

I use this mostly in my kitchen, near the sink, or when playing with my son or cleaning. Waterproof is definitely a bonus in those situations as I have lost other electronics, due to an errant splash, before.

It is pretty easy to use and connect, and I did so, with my iPad mini, without bothering with the instructions.

It comes with a strap, which is very handy. I keep this hanging from a cabinet knob when I'm working and I can hang it on a coat hook near the rest of my chargers, for charging.

The sound isn't the greatest. I think the materials definitely dampen it a bit. I prefer the sound from my Bose Wave or from my Philips iPod/iPhone dock, but neither of those offer the security of such durable housing, so it is a trade off I will gladly make.

review_text:
I suppose preference or hate for this seat will really come down to how you feel about basic car seats.

No, this isn't the fanciest or even I daresay best on the market, but it's a solid car seat that will do its job. I've used an older model of the Graco Snugride in the past and had no complaints or issues with that, and I feel about the same so far with this one, with a specific nod to the based, which I find fits, at least for me, better in the car.

review_title: Spend your money on a more reliable unit.
review_text:
Two SIGNIFICANT flaws with this unit:

When it's working properly, however, the sound quality is excellent, even at high volume - that is, about as good as you could get from a speaker this size. Which is why this is a 3-star instead of a 2-star review. But if you're going to spend this much money, you may as well spend it on something that will actually be reliable and function as intended.

product_name: NcStar Tactical Green Dot Scope Built-In Red Laser
review_title: Exceptional optic if you put it together correctly!
review_text:
Bought one and encountered the same problem that has plagued some one-star reviewers. The green dot and the laser both lost power after a dry fire, never mind putting live rounds downrange. Being somewhat of a troubleshooter, I found that tightening the battery terminal cap obviated that problem. It looks fragile, but as long as you don't cross the threads you can cinch it up pretty firmly without worrying about stripping it.

On test firing, windage was dead center, but the elevation was 3" high at 25 yards on the first group. Setting the BZO was thus very straightforward and afterwards it made for a fun evening annihilating the gallon jugs I've been stashing in my garage for the express purpose of shooting them.

For such an inexpensive optic, I'm perfectly happy with it after feeding a few mags through my AR with it on top. After cinching down the battery cap more tightly, the power loss issue didn't make an encore appearance. My only gripe is that the tri-rail 'armor' makes this sight an extremely cumbersome piece of gear on top of a 16" barrel AR. I'd prefer a blank piece of aluminum up top (doesn't need more tacti-cool crap hanging off of it) or a more robust casing that doesn't need an extra piece of metal screwed onto it to protect against rough handling.

review_text: I enjoyed this when I first received it. I plugged it in to my laptop and it auto downloaded what few albums I had( only about 10 or 12). The sound was OK for what I wanted which was to listen to a little music while I was working in the yard. I'm an old timer so I'm not fussy about buds too much as long as the sound is pretty good I'm ok with it. But then I bought some new music and tried to transfer it to the Evo but ....nothing. I get no Kubic icon when I hook it up to the laptop so Drag n' Drop is unavailable to me. The "upgrade library" feature doesn't upgrade...nothing transfers. So I'm stuck with the same original songs that I started with. Someone suggested that I load music from Amazon but I don't really see how to do that without the Drop n' Drag option, unless somebody in here can steer me right. The radio feature is good....if you're sitting in the same spot, if you move around at all you lose the station. So I liked it at first....a lot actually, it did what I wanted it to do. Until it didn't. I contacted Kubik to see if they could help but no answer yet. If nothing soon, I'll be looking for a different device. Too bad cause this one was pretty cool.....for a bit. So now I'm looking for a new item that will serve my simple expectations and last longer with the option to add some new music now and then. I would not recommend buying this. Since I wrote this I have played around with an old laptop I have that runs on Windows 7 and lo and behold, I can load music on this with the old laptop so now it isn't a total loss for me. I like the device in every other way other than the fact that without the ability to load music, to be able to open the folders, it is pretty much useless. So now I can use the old laptop for that purpose. I'm not changing the review though because I contacted Kubik and they never got to me. So the final word is it works on Windows 7 but not on Windows 8.

It is a colorful set (so you can easily spot them where you put them down) with adjustable ear hooks that actually worked pretty well (I thought that was pretty novel). The small clip is handy to keep the plug from accidentally pulling out of your MP3 player, but can be moved anywhere on the cord. It also came with a small mesh bag (standard type) and 3 sets of ear buds.

I couldn't believe the sound when I first put them in and tried them out!

They were *SO BAD*. While the mid-range was okay, there was a extreme lack of bass, like if you pulled the bass EQ down all the way and were only left with mid-high range. Usually when I push the earbuds in with my fingertips, the sound/bass improve dramatically as the seal gets better. Not so with these, the sounds gets more muffled and goes away. Later on in the day, I figured out that if I hold the ear hooks a certain way, the sound gets a lot lot better, esp. the bass, as the ear holes are better directed to my ear drums. Ah, that must be it. As the ear pieces are molded, it basically shoots the sound right into the wall of my ear canal and not my tympanic membrane. But rather than blame my myself, I realize that these are the only earbuds I've ever owned that I've had that problem, including another pair of Philips sport ear buds that work just fine (I also tested them against Amazon basic, and Onkyo earbuds.) Unfortunately, I can't exercise or do anything active while I hold the earhooks at just the right angle to listen. Or I could just accept the fit as is and forgo any kind of bass response. Maybe your ear canals are better suited for this set... but like I said, I've never had this issue before with other earphones.

I have to start off by saying I am not a fan of the Wrangler brand. But these jeans - they just might have made a believer out of me.
-

I have never liked them.
-
But - this pair you're looking at here - not too shabby. I'm a 34"x30", straight up. But when wearing boots, I need a 32" leg. I put these on and they fit well around the waist. But they're a bit baggy down below. The page here doesn't say, but these are definitely "boot cut" - they're pretty big on the ends there, and they're awfully long, for me. I usually need a 32" leg for boots, but these hit the floor, even with my boots on. They fit well in the waist-area, but the legs are baggy. Which, I suppose, is good for working. The jeans also have these little pockets behind the right knee - good for jamming a tool in there when you have nowhere else to put it. There's also a little hanger-thing on the left leg for a hammer. I'm sure there's a name for it - shows you what I know about blue-collar work. Hey - there's a reason why my sink leaks, ok!?!!
-
The material isn't smooth denim - it's a little rough but still comfortable. For the price, these are a really nice pair for working in.

This is very compact so it is quite inconspicuous. The other thing I like about this switch compared to my other one is that you can control it either with the controller or the on the device itself. The other one I have is controller only and if you have kids you know that controllers are rarely easy to be found. My only complaint, which is tiny, is that the controller does not include a battery.

We wanted this because when we set up our flat screen we had designed the area so that no cords would be showing and we ran the HDMI through the wall along with the TV power cord so we had a nice clean look. When we set this up we had a wireless DVD player but then we upgraded to 3D and needed a new DVD player which meant we had to have a HDMI cable running to the TV and we no longer had the nice clean look we were hoping to achieve. We got this and we were able to plug in our DVD player and Home theater system and run it out to our hidden HDMI cable and now we are back to no more cables hanging on our wall from our TV.

The picture is great with this too. And now we don't have to switch our TV input over to DVD when we want to watch it.

There are a couple ways to switch devices with this. There are arrow buttons on the remote so you can go back and forth or if you know the number of the devices you can just press the number on the remote or like I said above if you can't find the remote you can always change it on the switcher.

review_title: I Love the BEWM - But Inability to Find a Specific Source for Additional Replacement Cords Worries Me
review_text:
I like the bass drop, and if you like to crunk to BEWM, these certainly have the goods. In that respect, this has my full five star recommendation. However, I am still not convinced that being able to replace the cable is an efficient option, yet I can see the attraction for those really rough on cords. Also saves on having to "break in" new earbuds when you already have a pair you love (this break in period is also known as "burn time", making audio richer and fuller the more you listen to them).

If your cable (not the earbuds) goes wonker-doodles, do a search for "repacement earphone cable", different options pop up ... some of which seem to cost more than these headphones alone. I did a search to see if any specific replacement cables are available from Audiosharp or Sur S520 (the actual model number) directly, and couldn't find anything via Amazon. An extra cable comes with it, yet I would dearly like to have a concrete source for yet more of the same cables - this is the one star hit. Now it is possible one of the other options, like from Shure (no relation) or such will fit, but without confirmation, it would be a dice toss.

If anyone, consumer or Audiosharp themselves, can direct me to a source of replacement cables for this model: Sur S520, let me know, and I would be happy to note it and up to five stars.

product_name: RECARO Performance Coupe 2015 Infant Car Seat
review_text:
Looks like we're not the only consumers having the same issue of the seat not being able to detach from the base.

We've had 2 such failures in the span of a 6 month period. We're now on our 3rd (2nd replacement) of the car seat. The first incident occurred straight out of the box (on the third attach / detach) and we were able to promptly return to Amazon for a replacement. Not soon after getting our replacement (within 3 months) did we experience the same issue once again. After getting this second failure, I did some research and seems like this issue is starting to become prevalent on this model. On both failures, there were no straps, debris, etc. that would prevent the detachment of the seat from the base so this is obviously a design defect.

I've read reviews where Recaro required a video along with the S/N, P/N, and manufacture date. In reading these reviews, I went ahead and took numerous pictures along with videos showing the issue before contacting Recaro. It took me a couple of tries on different days and was able to contact them via their online chat on a Friday afternoon (about 2 PM PST). The customer service rep was polite and did not require me to send videos / pictures of the issue but I did mention this was the second time with the failed attach / detach. I gave all the required info S/N, P/N, and manufacture date to her right then and there and she mentioned Recaro will either send a replacement or refund my money. We decided to get a replacement since we bought the seat as part of a travel system with the stroller. Once our baby boy has outgrown the seat, we'll end up using the stroller. Our replacement seat is not currently being used as we've decided to use another brand by Simple Parenting. The replacement seat will be our backup for now as the reliability is only good for 3 months or so.

All in all, we thought the quality and reliability of Recaro was well known but obviously not for their child seat division, especially for the Performance Coupe model. Also, one last comment - their "Made in USA" statement is a little bit of a misnomer as there are some components that are foreign made. From what I understand, you can claim made in USA provided the majority of the components are domestically sourced while some percentage can be foreign sourced. Technically, it's better stated to claim "Assembled in USA" than "Made in USA."

product_name: Panasonic RP-BTGS10-A Premium Bluetooth Wireless Water-Resistant Open-Ear Headphones
review_title: Heavy. Uncomfortable. Too quiet. Poorly designed. But nice concept. (Or, "earbuds vs RP-BTGS10")
review_text: 11/10/2015: I have updated my review by one star after using this item pretty much daily for the past few months. I still feel it is uncomfortable, and the volume is too low, and the battery compartment stuff is cheesy, but the convienience of not having cables is really nice. It also makes you look like a Borg with little ear pieces sticking out (but not covering your ears). I am sold on the concept of wireless headphones like this, but feel there is much room for improvement in design. I'd say: definately get something like this, but unless there is a great cost savings with this Panasonic model, look elsewhere.  Oh, Panasonic. Weren't you once a leader in electronics? The Panasonic arr pee dash bee tee gee ess ten (why are product names so awful)? is a great concept. I like the idea of the around-the-ear earphones rather than the traditional over-the-head type, and perhaps there is an advantage if the unit it light, but the RP-BTGS10 is not light. After a week of daily use, I still find it heavy and uncomfortable.  The unique feature of this Bluetooth headset is that it isn't actually earphones. Instead of two earbuds that go in your ear, there are two soft pads that press against your skull just in front of your ears, leaving your ears open to the outside sounds around you. I was thrilled at this concept, since when I listen to audio at work, I only put one earbud in so I can hear people sneaking up on me. (I still smile every time I have to pound outside someone's cube to get their attention while they have earbuds in and cranked up, only to see them jump with surprise when they realize I am there.) This part works surprisingly well -- but the volume, even at max, is too quiet if there is any background noise. I can't hear anything while water runs in the sink in the breakroom, for instance. So far, my "one earbud in, one earbud out" method is better for noisy surroundings.  The next feature, Bluetooth, is simply great. I have pretty much always used earbuds (except in my home studio where I use large headphones). I have gone through many pair of earbuds over the years as the cable would get snagged and eventually cause one bud to short out. Without wires, this problem wouldn't happen. RP-BTGS10 wins here.  The unit is powered by a AAA rechargable battery, and claims to get around 4 hours of playback, though I was able to get through most of a full work day. Battery life seems okay, but be prepared to buy a spare AAA to keep charged unless you want to stop mid-day and wait for the "about an hour" recharge time. The included USB charger has slots for two batteries, but they only provide one. I guess they like their customers being inconvienienced. I'm going to give earbuds the edge here since they never need batteries.  Speaking of batteries, the battery compartment is ridiculous. There is an outside flap you have to open, then it hangs loose on a small strand, and then there is the battery door you push down on to open up on a hinge. Really, Panasonic? The AAA battery then slides in ... but which way? In an absolutely brilliant (sarcasm) design, the small diagram that shows which way the battery gets inserted is covered up when you open the battery compartment. Have the design engineers at Panasonic ever seen an Apple product? They should spend some time looking around an Apple Store to see how these problems have been solved long ago.  This device is "one size fits all", and they provide two colors of the same size rubber bands you can put on to tighten it. The bands have loops at each end and are meant to slide to some tiny notches. I gave up using these quickly, as they made the unit painfully tight, and the bands just kept sliding back over the notch. Awful design here, too.  This is really a poorly designed product. However, I have been using it in place of my earbuds (except when charging) because (if the area is quiet) wireless is so much more convienient (except for the recharging) than wired earbuds. product_name: Paws & Pals Dog Pet Carrier Rolling Backpack Cat Easy Walk Travel Tote Premium Quality Airline Approved - Durable
review_text:
I’ve flown with my 17lb dachshund before with a handheld travel bag and I bought the OxGord so I could wheel her and also carry my own bag, thus avoiding the need to check anything. We’ve now flown twice with this plan and both trips went smoothly.

The OxGord rolling pet carriers have the same exterior dimensions as the medium Snoozer rolling bags, which have many reviews of successful carry-on plane travel. The OxGord is also a fraction of the price.

To stow this bag under-the-seat-infront-of-you, you have to remove the bottom structure of the bag. This can easily be done in the isle by detaching the velcro and removing the exterior floor. From the reviews I read, this is the same procedure for the Snoozer bag.

Pros:
- More mesh than our previous bag which kept Eva (our doxie) from getting hot and panting
- It works
- Very incognito, when Eva was in bag most people didn't notice I had a dog, including the person sitting next to me

Cons:
- Not sturdy, strong or stable - I definitely handled this bag with care, it feels very breakable, not made for any heavy use - especially with the added weight of Eva I avoided uneven ground and curbs, I also only lifted it by the nylon handles and not the metal retractable
- No interior padding - I added a thin pillow that we usually use in her kennel, without that addition she would have been extremely uncomfortable flying for 3hrs
- Retractable handle sticks - which worried me but luckily it didn't stick at any crucial moment like security or boarding

FYI:
Standard airline under seat dimensions
22" deep x 14" wide x 9" heigh

OxGord Rolling Travel Carrier
14" (Length) x 11" (Width) x 19" (Height)

product_name: Panasonic Best in Class Noise Cancelling
review_title: Fair headphones with minimal noise cancelling
review_text:
Panasonic RPHC56K Headphones

This kit includes the basics of a travel based headphone set. It had the in ear headphones with a battery driven noise canceller. It also has three pairs of ear buds to fit your size (S-M-L), an airliner adapter plug and a soft pouch to carry it all. There is also an included “heavy duty” AAA battery but I’d advise using an Alkaline.

The headphones do not work at all without using the power-pack which also has some noise-cancelling ability. I haven’t taken them on an airplane trip but in normal operation I don’t really notice much. The power-pack has the on-off switch with a volume slider. Interestingly the volume slider does not go to full off, the sound is there and there are no controls so you have to get to the player/phone to pause or change tracks, an annoyance.

The sound quality to me is average. It’s not awful but it isn’t that good. I used my set of songs I test headphones with and it wasn’t unpleasant but I wasn’t soaring musically in my head. All in all an average set of earbuds with an above average price.

Finding a fit isn't difficult and with more headphones of this type offering this \\"memory wire\\" it becomes easy to find what works best for pretty much anyone. It also helps I think to make them a little more comfortable.
With a claim of 8 hours of battery life they seem to offer a nice long time between charging. I do not listen to music or talk on the phone very often at all so I really cannot say with 100% certainty how that aspect plays out. Just wanted to be up front on that one, there is no time when I have the need or desire to spend a prolonged time talking to anyone or listening to anything but I do like that I can snag a headset on the way out the door and not worry about it being charged. That gives a plus to the battery life but also a negative to the size, guess you can't have it all.
Voice prompts are always preferred (I think) to a bunch of beeps or LED flashes to offer status updates and these offer that.
Pretty decent range and but the buttons aren't very easy to use and have register being presse d every time I found. If bass isn't a big deal and you just want something to toss on when at the gym these might work for you but with so many options on the market maybe not!

review_title: Clean and open sound, better than they have any right to be at their price.
review_text:
It is probably redundant to add another five star review here, but I am highly impressed. These were purchased strictly for music. I am very old school (and probably very old) and listen to all of my music collection in stereo. I received the Sound Sommeliers last Monday, so this review is based on only seven days worth of listening, about twenty hours. However, in that time, I have some very firm opinions of the capabilities of these little speakers.

One (and most impressive), amazingly open. The sound is like that of one of the older dipole speakers like the original Quad Electrostatic or three panel Magnaplanars. When you pull the speakers into your room a minimum of 18" to 24" from the walls, the speakers honestly disappear and you hear only the music. No localization. Simply wonderful sound from beyond the boundaries of the speakers in both the lateral as well as the front to back planes. This is most true on acoustic music and vocals, but also comes through well on electric music. Symphonic music is not handled quite as well (I don't think). Have only listened to a few favorites here and the material was tough for any speaker.

Two, very good bass response down to about 50hz. I have not had the desire to connect any of two available sub-woofers to the setup which could extend the bass down to 20hz-25hz range. The bass is open and fast via the 3-1/2" full range driver and I have seen the addition of a sub-woofer actually muddy the sound of some full range speakers. I plan to live with these units for a while (at least a year) prior to any decision to extend the bass. Besides, on most recording, there is very little output below 40hz anyway so unless you know you are looking for some extremely deep output, you probably won't be missing much.

Three, articulate treble response. I am unfamiliar with the full range driver, but it is surprising that it has response that has such good midrange and upper midrange/lower treble response. At my age, I know I have little hearing above the 5khz-7khz range, so extended treble response is relatively unimportant. If someone in their twenties were to tell me these roll-off treble response, I can stand corrected on this. However, my wife's hearing is still pretty good (according to hearing tests, not me) and she likes what she hears and doesn't think the units are missing anything. She also likes that they don't seem to get sibilant on voices, cymbals and other instruments that sometimes bother her.

Four, WAF. Yup, the good old Wife Acceptance Factor. These are so slight that they pass most WAF's with flying colors. Not only that, easy to hide when not in use and if you want some background music, sound is acceptable up against a wall.

What's not to like.

Received mine with one top end cap off. Cut myself attempting to get it back on. My bad. Should have sent it back but didn't want to wait.

Wish they came with a stable base.

Absolute volume is not very loud without some distortion. Still loud enough to enjoy most music. If you are young and you still want to put on something and "CRANK IT UP", you better look somewhere else.

Nice job K&B.

By the way, these are being used instead of Infinity Interlude IL-40's matched with Infinity sub-woofers which are now officially in the closet (subs had been in the closet since sometime in 2012). product_name: Grado Prestige Series SR325e Headphones
review_title: Game changer for old school audiophile
review_text:
For 25 years i believed that in order to have audiophile quality sound you needed a good home system and great SPEAKERS. After owning the grado SR325e's for a month or so (and a good break in period) I now believe that it is possible with HEADPHONES! I like to hear details and balanced sound (not too much bass, or to hot in treble). Of course this is subjective, but I'll try to describe what I've experienced. For about 14 years my headphones were sony mdr7506. Maybe i got use to their sound signature and thought it was good enough. They seemed detailed and some good bass with lively punch. However, i would usually tire of listening to them and feel the treble was a little shrill. Also the music soundstage? Sounded a bit distant compared to the grado that makes you feel almost in the middle of the performance! After a few months i tried to go back and listen to the sonys...i was almost sickened to think at one point i told several friends and even facebook that the sonys were a great headphone. Maybe for their price they are ok. The 325e had more bass, great detailed highs that are seldom shrill, unless listening to poor cd,file,or equipment. What am i trying to say?? These headphones WILL REVEAL weaknesses in source recording and equipment. They won't gloss over, they will give a clear reproduction. The upshot? If you have good equipment and sources YOU WILL BE REWARDED with almost blissful sound and hear your recordings as if for the first time. Especially if you've had budget headphones before.

Now, my grado experience started at the store listening to sr60, sr80 and sr125e's. I decided since the sony 7506 were about $90 I'd shoot a bit higher in price and started with the sr125e grado's at home. I spent a good week or two playing music through them while I was at work. I know they say not to play them continuously, so I made a cd with about 30 min silence and 40 min or misc. music. believe me breaking in the headphones HELPS!! don't judge them right out of the box. it took about 50 hours or so until they mellowed out enough in the treble to sound nice. remember I'm talking about the sr125e's right now. I'm not sure if they seemed bass heavy and treble shy for my tastes. I kept thinking "there has got so be more stuff i'm not hearing in this recording" like ambience decay of reverb etc... so, before my 30 day trial was up I returned the SR125e's to the store and picked up the SR325e's because I had been reading that the 325's or more detailed or brighter...and one review said "not in a bad way".

So, now you should know that ALL grado headphones are OPEN BACKED so they WILL NOT block out much if any outside noise. so if you want to block out sound or use them in noisy places YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. I believe the open backed design helps facilitate a VERY sensitive response to music signals and the driver moves very easily. this results in good bass, but detailed harmonics. you feel like you hear almost every nuance within the sounds. it is very easy to focus on just a guitar part and hear all the subtle timbre characteristics. maybe I used that word wrong?? lol cymbals splash and swish and oscillate. they don't go "shhhhh" or "pshhhhh". I can hear background singers DISTINCTLY!! one annoying thing is you can also hear engineering mistakes and over compression distortion very easily. thankfully its not obvious on all recordings, but my 2014 led zep II remaster is hard to listen to, but I realize that is what it is... sometimes I wonder if certain high frequencies are a little over pronounced or the response not as smooth as they might be in higher models, but that only shows up every now and then....

some people complain about the comfort of the grado headphones. I will not say they are bad, but they sound so good I am willing to fiddle with them every now and then to stay comfortable. the sr125e had flat pads that seemedto block some of the treble and got irritating kinda quick. while the sr325e come with L-cush pads which I liked better. I LOVE THE CORD its kinda big, but the best part is ALMOST NO NOISE when cable moves across clothes or hits something. plug is 1/8" with 1/8 to 1/4" adapter

I am preparing myself to upgrade to the PS1000e in the future! and this is coming from a guy who NEVER thought great audiophile sound could be had from headphones...until now.

in conclusion I WHOLEHEARTEDLY recommend grado SR325e for audiophile type listeners that like detailed sound that is not overly heavy on bass. if you want a rolled off treble and strong bass check out the sr125e'sle and got irritating kinda quick. while the sr325e come with L-cush pads which I liked better. review_title: but decided on 4 because so many people seem too think these are going to be the best pair of headphones in the world
review_text:
I wavered between giving these 4 or 5 stars, but decided on 4 because so many people seem too think these are going to be the best pair of headphones in the world.
I've been using these for years. Various pairs. Never had a pair break on me, but I do lose the plastic ear pieces. They like to fall off a lot. And if they pick up crap from hanging out in the bottom of your bag (hey, they cost 6 bucks!), they're impossible to clean.

The sound is very good to me. I'm not an audiophile by any means, but I am a professional classical musician, and I listen to a lot of opera, so when I'm casually listening these definitely work. I don't really pay attention to bass. I do have a nicer pair of Thinksound Rain earbuds i use sometimes that are an eensy bit better in terms of sound quality, but i'm not an audiophile, so I'm not good at telling these things.

Comfort- my main qualm. I'm not a fan of the hard plastic housing. It makes my ears sore. After years of putting up with it (it's not that bad), I'm on the hunt for a more comfortable pair of earbuds.

Definitely buy these. They're 6 bucks! And very good. And don't break! But, they're not revolutionary headphones or something. They won't do your laundry and make you hotter, jeez.

review_title: Don't bother with these flat ones.
review_text: Bought this antenna to replace one that had the dipoles on it (rabbit ear style) that fell and broke. I bought it because of the better reviews and it was inexpensive. Well, our broken one worked better than this and it wasn't amplified. I live in an area with lots of trees and houses close together and don't have a direct line of sight to the towers in my area. I tried placing this antenna in many locations and angles and it would just not work with out the picture going out constantly, it was in a room with a window view facing the direction of the TV transmission towers. I really don't think the amp worked at all. The LED light never came on unless the coax connector from the antenna was not connected I even tried it with our old one and it made no difference. I ended up returning it and bought an amplified one that has the 2 dipole antennas on it (RCA ANT1251), I didn't buy it from Amazon, but it works really good. This flat style antenna might work for some people that are closer and have an unobstructed view of the TV transmission towers but if you question your signal strength you might want to look at some others first.

product_name: Banana Boat Sport Performance Sunscreen Lotion
review_text: First review ever, but I needed others to know about my experience with this product. Wore it today for the first time, and 10 minutes into my walk, I was already sweating profusely, and through my customary 2 hours walk, I was soaked all over as if my own personal cloud was raining on me unbeknownst to others. My situation is this: sure, I was out on the South Florida heat (morning, however, but it does get pretty hot nowadays), and sure, I walk at a fast pace; but I've been doing it every single day for the past 7 months, and using Hawaiian Tropic, and I can definitely tell you that I am below average in the sweating scale - never has anything close to this happened to me. The only reason I changed sunscreen was because I wouldn't pay 13 dollars for the Hawaiian Tropic I last (before the advent of Summer) bought for 4. I don't know if I got some faulty batch, or what, and I'd be more than willing to ship it back to the manufacturer if they want to find out. If this is normal for this product, I don't understand how a sport sunscreen can cause immoderate sweating so that it will absolutely skim off in no time whatsoever. Also, I couldn't understand all the positive reviews, unless everyone uses this staying pretty still around the pool or in the beach - which could be the case. So, if this is normal, and if you're planning on moving more than 100 feet per hour or so, I would recommend you not to buy this, not even to accept it as a gift. I most eagerly wish to speak with the vendor or the manufacturer - this product was a waste of 6 dollars, but, much more regrettably, it ruined one of my morning walks, which I won't ever get back.

product_name: Cat Dancer 101 Cat Dancer Interactive Cat Toy
review_title: Please be careful if you do buy this
review_text:
It's amazing how such a simple device can make my cats go crazy. The thing about this one is that you have to be REALLY CAREFUL when playing with it. Never, ever leave it out when you're done, and that should go for any kind of cat toys with long stringy parts. When playing with this, don't let your cats chomp down on the wire. I try to hold it at a length where the cats can bat around the cardboard part at the end, but not get their paws or mouth on the wire. It takes practice and a very watchful eye, but that's the only safe way to use this toy. There's a small, sharp hook at the end, where the wire was bent to hold the cardboard on. I can see how that could easily rip through a cat's cheek or paw pad like a fishing hook. Also, if they're jumping for it, sometimes the wire gets caught between their little fingers. I can't imagine that feels good.

So, two stars because all three of my cats go nuts for it. It even gets my old, lazy one off the couch. But it does make me worry that less-informed cat parents might not realize how dangerous it is. At the end of the day, I couldn't recommend this to anyone.

review_text: OK, so I bought these the other day on Amazon Prime Day for $19.99 on a lightening deal. I've been wanting to try Bluetooth earbuds for awhile now, but not wanting to spend some of the rediculous prices some ask for them. I just got them today, and am quite pleased so far with my initial experience with them. These are very nice and come with some good accessories that allow you to customize them for the way you would like to wear and use them. They have assorted sized little rubber tips that allow you to find the right size for your ears. Also included are two sets of these little rubber stabilizers which help you to insure they will stay put in your ear. These are very soft and are easily positioned in your ear without feeling odd.finally the are also the little ear hooks you can put on if you want 100 percent assurance they won't fall of while doing rigorous exercise for example. The box also contains a little clip whic attaches to the cord that you can then clip to your shirt, or maybe even to a hat, so if they do fall,out of both your ears (unlikely, but possible), or if you want to take them both out to have a conversation with someone, the whole set won't fall to the ground, but will be held in place. Nice idea. In addition, they have these two  little plastic pieces with little grooves in them which allow you to shorten the length of the cord if you find it to be too long. Also in the box is a charging cable and a nice little pouch to hold everything in! I had some weeding to do, so paired them with my iPhone, very quickly, no problem, and went out to weed. I wore them with the cord behind my head. It's pretty easy to feel the 3 control buttons and know which one is which, and use them. The controls work great allowing volume up and down, pause and play, skip forward or back thru songs. Volume and sound quality is very good. They stayed put in my ears, except the right one would loosen up a bit, but didn't fall out. I think it's because the control switch is on the right side so there's a bit of extra weight pulling on that side, as well as when you adjust the volume or skip a track your tugging a bit on that right side as a result of using it. review_title: I do think it is a good quality food and my cat ate it and enjoyed ...
review_text: Although I give this 3 stars, I do think it is a good quality food and my cat ate it and enjoyed it for several years. Unfortunately he just suffered from a urinary blockage and a partial blockage a month ago and his diet will need to change. I thought I was doing great feeding him a grain free, quality, food, but after researching, I am wondering if there are just too many things in some of these types of foods that cats just don't need or are actually counterproductive to their health. For instance, there are almost a dozen fruits and vegetables listed in this food + potato flour. Cats get a minute amount of veggies in the wild and need mostly an all meat diet. Sounds great and healthy to us but do our cats actually need spinach and carrots? The answer is no. I also read that some of the senior foods (as well as all drys) have even more of an impact on a cat maintaining proper hydration, which can lead to blockage issues in males. An all wet or raw diet if really the best. If my female cat likes this dry, I will probably feed the rest to her with wet as well. But our male will be on a prescription diet as he transitions to all wet  Also, as someone else mentioned, for some reason only half of this food would get eaten by my cat. Lots of it ended up on the floor outside of the bowl, so there can be some waste. I appreciate company's that try to make more quality pet foods, I'm just not sure some of the ingredients are of benefit, and may even be detrimental.

product_name: L'Oreal Paris Cosmetics Voluminous Miss Manga Rock Mascara
review_text:
I’ve been wanting to try this manga mascara for a while now. The packaging and the container look so cool and getting those “manga” lashes are worth trying something new.

The Feel: The mascara goes on smooth and clean, but the short little bristles make it clump and feel awkward. To make it feel okay for me, I had to use an eyelash curler and a separate eyelash brush to separate my lashes. I suppose this is the trick to getting manga eyelashes, to stick them together, but it felt very uncomfortable. I can see using this on fake lashes and being okay. The mascara didn't irritate my eyes, but it messed with the lashes so that it was uncomfortable and I kept messing with them all day.

The Look: There is definitely a very graphic, manga look when wearing this mascara. After putting some on one eye and not the other, I observed my eye looked more open and alert. A few observers that did not know what I had put on it, said one eye looked awake and the other asleep. So the look, is definitely a plus if you want that big lash feel.

Overall: I won’t be getting this again. Although the look is great and the mascara itself is of nice quality, the brush making my lashes stick together was not comfortable. I don’t want a mascara I have to use two other products to apply. Like I said, if you are using fake lashes, this may be the best product out there.
