product_name: SanDisk  Clip Jam MP3 Player
review_title: If time is not an issue, feel free to waste your time on this.
review_text: This is the third review I have given on this product (my original reviews have seem to have mysteriously vanished), and my opinion on it continues to deteriorate.  DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME, DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS PIECE OF CRAP.  You could spend your time with your lover, you could spend your time at a fine restaurant, you could spend your time with a good book or a video, but if you buy this crap you will waste your time on it.  I continuously try to load play lists onto it that are in a specific order.  While my laptop says the songs are on the device, the device says they are not, and I have to repeat the process all over untill it works.  It is very finicky.  I would throw this thing against the wall in frustration (I am on my fourth attempt at loading a play list) but I go to sea next week and I need something for the treadmill. No other purchase will get to me in time for when we shove off on deployment, so I am stuck with this as I try to make it work.  I have never experienced as much frustration with something as I have with this.  Trying to make a custom playlist took TOOOOO long.  First you have to load what you want into a folder on your computer, then move the contents of the folder into the computer's player, arrange the order in the computer player, then save the play list back to the original folder as a playlist, then move the folder with the songs and the playlist to the clip player.  There were times when the computer would show the songs and the list in the folder moved to the clip jam, but the clip jam would say the play list was empty and would not play.  If you want songs in a particular order, and there are a lot of them, it can be a labor intensive process re-arranging them in your computer player before saving them as a custom playlist, but the final transfer to the clip player was not always successful.  I am too busy to waste this kind of time.  Good that all it does is play audio - nice for runs; good sound; DEFINITELY NOT USER FRIENDLY.  MORE, two days later.  DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY.  THIS IS A TOTAL PIECE OF JUNK.  I went in to edit one of my playlists, and now it will not read the new one.  It says that playlist is "empty" but the computer says there are files in that folder.  I have spent over an hour trying to add one song to a list.  SanDisk really botched this one up - it does not work; your frustration factor will go through the roof.

They're more versatile, and the sound quality is as good as any, plus two separate sets allow me to take one to my office. Our son has Bose, and our grandson has Beats, and both agree that Silent Safari is as good as either I agree on both counts. Hopefully, our problem was just an abberation, and the new set will last for years. Thank you Silent Safari.

You can use it as a revitalizer after a day of being out and your curls let go, but I use it as a styling product in the morning. The smell is wonderful and a big bottle of this is going to last me a very long time. One tip, use sparingly on your hair until you know how much to use. Too much makes your hair slightly oily. review_title: Fine for Bluetooth  but the volume will not adjust from maximum if using the auxiliary input jack
review_text:
I purchased this as a remote speaker for a television set. My mother is hard of hearing, and placing a speaker closer to her would allow the TV volume to be kept at a more reasonable level. I selected the Amazon unit as it had a 3.5 mm jack so I could hard wire it to the TV via the TV's headphone jack. I got the first unit and plugged it in to the TV only to discover the unit was at its maximum volume and could not be adjusted either from the volume controls on the unit or the TV. I returned it for another unit with the same problem occurring. But, this time I then tried using it after pairing the unit to my Fire telephone. When used as a Bluetooth device, the volume could be adjusted and the tone was excellent for a speaker at this price. So, this is a good buy for use with Bluetooth, but worthless for use with the auxiliary jack.

Update - I purchased a JBL Flip 2 as a replacement. It was well worth the extra dollars. Not only does the volume adjustment work when using the 3.5 mm input jack, the JBL unit comes with the wall charger (the Amazon unit does not) and a carrying case.

product_name: Summer Infant Extra Camera for Sharp Sight High Definition Video Baby Monitor (29340)
review_text:
It's been years since my children were infants and even my grandchildren are past that stage (at least for now) but I still have use for this item. I have a new pet cockatiel and even though I work just 100 yards away from my home I thought that if I could check up on him and even hear him whistle I would feel better about him being alone all day.

Set up of the camera and monitor couldn't have been easier. After both are plugged in and the camera is turned on you hold the power button on the monitor for about 4 seconds and it syncs easily and automatically (at least it did for me). The picture is sharp and clear. The sound is just so-so but it is good enough for what it is made for. I love that it can be turned so that you can see the entire room. It is almost a 360 degree view. The temperature monitoring is also important, especially for tropical birds. If it gets to cold due to a power outage he could be in big trouble.

I sometimes talk to my bird via this monitor while I am at work. He doesn't talk back yet but we will work on that.

product_name: SmartyKat Hot Pursuit Cat Toy Concealed Motion Toy
review_title: while after these fixes it's an awesome cat toy
review_text:
This review explains solutions to problems that are common with this. I still left it at 3 stars, because, while after these fixes it's an awesome cat toy, I still had to DO these in the first place to make it usable, which I find ridiculous.

This toy has a MAJOR FLAW - the motor will shut off if your cat holds the wand for 5-10 seconds.

For me, this meant that I basically had to sit there with the toy as he played with it, turning it back on every 15ish seconds. I was hoping to use this to distract him while I was doing homework, so this flaw rendered it essentially useless. My cat would trigger the turn-off, and then start howling because the toy wasn't playing with him anymore.
But I found a trick to this. If you put the base on a turntable (lazy susan), the base spins while your cat holds the wand. Eventually, my cat lets go for a second to attack it again, and it spins around again. A turntable made this toy do exactly what it's supposed to do, and now my cat plays with it for as long as I'll let him.
The second problem I found is that my cat pulls the wand off. I only use the feather wand (it comes with two), so this isn't a big problem for me. I just epoxied the wand onto the little attacher piece.
The third problem (which isn't a problem for me, but is for some cats I'd imagine) is the motor is a bit loud. My cat doesn't mind, and he seems to be more interested in it because of the noise, but it might be an issue for you.

With these two solutions, this toy will become awesome for any cat that doesn't mind a little motor noise.

The turntable I bought. Fits the base perfectly, so there's no slipping/sliding on the turntable.

product_name: TEAC NP-H750 USB DAC / Network Player Integrated Amplifier, 20Hz-60kHz Frequency Response, 40W + 40W Output Power, AirPlay, USB Streaming, Wi Fi Certified
review_title: This thing seems to do everything
review_text: I needed an audio system for a work area. I already owned a pair of speakers so thought an integrated amplifier would be the appropriate choice. I store my music on a Mac Mini and this can be connected to an amplifier through the headphone connection. I looked at many integrated amplifiers hoping that a review would lead me to a good choice. I became interested in the amplifiers that would work as a DAC particularly the Teac AH-01. I thought I might get better reproduction by not using the headphone output on the Mini. I looked at the Teac NP-H750 and thought that accessing my home network and internet radio stations would be a nice plus. When I saw it on sale I decided to buy it and have been very pleased with the purchase. My first impression was that this a very well built item. The unit itself is very nicely made. The unit and particularly the knobs are very solid. The unit is a nice compact size. The remote is very solid and good looking. Setting up the unit was pretty straight forward. The instruction book was very clearly written. Entering my network password was a bit slow because you have to scroll through upper and lower case as well as digits but you only do this once. I went to the site listed in the directions and downloaded the Teac Radio Guide to my computer. This allows you to select stations using the controls of a computer instead of making due with the controls on the Teac and sends the information to the Teac. This made selecting internet radio stations much, much easier. You can try stations and if not satisfied easily delete them. Connecting directly to my Mac Mini was a little more of a challenge. First you have to download and install some software. This procedure is listed at the front of the instruction manual before the basic set up procedure and easy to miss. The unit, since it works with Apple Air Play wanted to use that instead of the direct feed from the computer. It's necessary to go to the system preferences on the computer and select the USB over the headphone output. Through a little trial and error I got it working and was pleased with the results. I have found the sound produced in all modes to be very satisfactory. I'm not an audiophile but have decent audio equipment and believe this unit to be quite good. All in all I have found the Teac NP-H750 to be a very good quality, very versatile, good sounding unit. I haven't tried it at high volumes and suspect by the output rating it might be limited in that regard. Perhaps someone else will comment on that.

review_text: I decided to cut subscription cable and try OTA HDTV. I'm not too happy with the results. I'm about 25 miles from the broadcast towers and I'm lucky if I can pick up even one of the 3 major broadcast channels. I even connected my TV directly to the antenna to rule out splitter/wiring issues and got similar results. Weather seems to have a lot to do with it. On a cloudy day I tend to receive more channels, but it's not a certainty. One morning I started receiving a channel I've never been able to pick up before, and then a day or two later it stopped coming in again. Very inconsistent and somewhat disappointing. Maybe it will work better with winter weather?

review_title: Kind of bummed because this gate started out great! Very sturdy and it was in a place ...
review_text:
Kind of bummed because this gate started out great! Very sturdy and it was in a place in our house that we didn't need to put it up and take it down a lot, it was meant to be pretty permanent at least until our kid got older. We have had a lot of baby gates over the years, and its easy to set up, we use the pressure mounting method so as to not damage our antique wood trim in all of our doorways by screwing holes into them. Like I said, started out great, then gradually over the course of maybe 3 weeks the pressure holding it up weakened somehow. I do know that it was the gate, and not our doorway widening under the pressure, because even holding the lever down (which is how the pressure is applied when you set it up) it would no longer stay up. I cannot explain it, and don't really understand it. Even when I tried a higher pressure setting which actually made my doorway creak and sound like I was breaking the wood, the gate just fell down once I set the lever into place. Something inside the gate is not working properly, and it was in the beginning. I have kept it in a closet in case I am able to somehow use it for something in the future, but it was not a good purchase as far as I can tell. The cheap-o wooden pressure mounted gates are what seems to still work best in our house.

If you decided to use the other mounting methods which involve screwing into the wall, this gate might be better.

product_name: SMSL SA-60 60WPC Class D Digital Amplifier silver
review_text:
In my quest to complete my whole home stereo system (which is really just a trial and error exercise for various gadgets amps speakers and cables) I've found myself in need of some compact muscle to fill in the gaps.

In my opinion this handsome little amp falls in the error column. It is a good looking little amp that's got some weight to it and feels solidly built but lacks any real power. I ran this amp side by side against the lepy 2024+ using various inputs and speakers both 4 and 8 ohms and the lepy beat this amp in every conceivable way (except looks maybe) at half the price.

Firstly this amp begins clipping at cuts out at volumes that the lepy cruises right on past. Both amps tend to clip when driving my 8 ohm klipsch speakers which I have a couple different models of but the lepy does so at far higher volumes then the smsl . When driving 4 ohm klipsch satellites the lepy drives them far past comfortable volumes and the smsl wimps out again. All the small amps I've tested do a way better job with 4 ohm speakers likely due to less resistance on their digital circuitry but the lepy leaves this amp in the dust.

The lack of any tone nobs makes this amp a far lessor option for a whole home rig because I don't really want to be making these adjustments on my computer because will affect the sound throughout my entire house.

The second input on both amps does not deliver a quality sound on either amp in comparison to the rca inputs but I guess that's to be expected and I've used other gadgets to eliminate the need for them but again the lepys second input delivers superior sound to the smsl delivered.

I'm no electrical engineer but I've been playing in bands for over 20 years and been listening to music since being in the womb and I trust what I hear. My advice would be to skip this purchase, get the lepy 2024 + and save yourself at least $30 in the process!

product_name: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphones with Memory Wire
review_title: Poor quality, gave them two chances
review_text:
I need this style of headphones for running, because the normal Apple earbuds will not stay in my ears. I had a pair of Philips sport headphones that I just loved until I blew out one of the speakers. Unfortunately that Philips model is discontinued, so I ordered these.

They fit in my ears great, and sounded great, too, but pretty soon I noticed that the slightest brush against the remote clicker would cause the sound to cut out in the right ear. Then the next day I tried them the headphones were constantly triggering Siri, like every 5 seconds. This made them essentially unusable, so I came here to get a return and leave a review, but then I noticed all the responses by customer service, so I figured I would give them a try.

Customer service was very attentive and immediately responded to all my emails. They sent me a new pair, which arrived today. I tried them on, but this time, instead of the clicker being too sensitive, the clicker does not work at all. I'm sure they would happily replace this pair, too, but 0 for 2 is not a very good record, so I'm not going to waste any more time with this model.

Another minus that should be mentioned is that the volume control is a passive slider, not a true remote volume control.

product_name: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphones with Memory Wire
review_title: Sweat problems with remote almost from the start
review_text:
I've used these first lightly when I received them last February (2014). I progressed to using them more and more from September or so, up till about two weeks ago when I decided that enough is enough and I'm looking to buy better earphones. Bought them with a group of friends through a third party that orders from Amazon in bulk and forwards to our country where Amazon doesn't ship electronics (Israel).

Pros:
These were great when I used these earphones running or walking in the autumn and the winter.
The music sounds clear, they're comfortable to wear most of the time and they're really light.

Cons:
The memory wire doesn't really keep in place properly, it needs adjustments every 15 minutes or so, but it's not so bad.
The clip that supposedly attaches to the shirt isn't strong enough so I didn't use it. The metal spring that holds it rusted from my sweat but it still holds. The problem with it is that when it's not attached firmly, it bounces and makes a lot of noise that makes it hard to hear the music that's playing.

The real problems started when the spring and summer approached. Running in a humid climate with 30+ degrees Celsius outside is what really did it for me - the sweat did enter the remote/microphone device, and it did do something wrong to the electronics inside. Maybe it's just mine that's faulty, but since the first time that it let the sweat go in, it takes a few minutes of playing with the volume control to make it play in both ears simultaneously. I wish it ended there, but it didn't. So now I put the remote inside my shirt when I run so that it doesn't bounce, and there it encounters the aforementioned sweat yet again. At several points, the sweat made it pause, rewind and forward the songs up to a point where I just turned the music off.
Another sweat problem is when it gets in your ear and makes the buds slide out. Guess they're not strong enough to stay inside when it gets wet :-(
And another small con is the volume control which is separate from the mp3 player's volume control. Maybe I just got used to remotes that controlled the player's volume, but I don't like it the way it is with this product.
Also, the microphone wasn't good from the start - it always transmits ambient noises too loudly making the other side not able to hear me.

product_name: Diono RadianRXT Convertible Car Seat, Daytona
review_title: Trying to tighten the straps? Forget about it.
review_text:
We've used this car seat for several months now and this is what we've determined:

Pros - Very sturdy and seems to be well built. We like the high back and the material is generally nice. It is convertible which is always a bonus.

Cons - For their life of me I have always had difficulty getting the straps tighter. Rear facing was a nightmare because when you are trying to ratchet the strap at the bottom of the seat to get it tighter the actual back seat in the car gets in the way so the angle is horrible for that. I thought it would get better once our son was front facing because the back seat wouldn't be in the way. That wasn't the case. For some reason it is so incredibly difficult to tighten the straps with the ratchet feature. And while it does seem very sturdy which is a bonus, it is also very heavy which makes it difficult if you need to move the seat to another car or travel in an airplane.

Overall there is more pain associated with this seat than I would have imagined. I wouldn't recommend this particular seat. My sister has a Diono but a different model and likes it. We got a Britax Marathon for our other car and like that much better.

product_name: Skippy Creamy Peanut Butter, 64 Ounce (Pack of 2)
review_title: In no way will I be referring to the nutrition label or ingredient list like many people do for these reviews
review_text:
First of all, this review has nothing to do with health factors of peanut butter or the “naturalness” of peanut butter. All this review is about is taste and quality. In no way will I be referring to the nutrition label or ingredient list like many people do for these reviews, just taste.
Skippy Peanut butter is always a favorite among kids and I remember having the tubes of Skippy peanut butter as a kid. You may ask yourself, what is the main reason for this? The answer is clear; Skippy is so much sweeter than any other peanut butter on the market that kids can’t get enough of it. But most of us college students want something more savory and that has that classic peanut butter taste. Skippy is simply just far too sweet to handle for me.
Another reason that I cannot handle Skippy is the texture. When I but creamy peanut butter, I expect creaminess. However, when I stuck a knife into the jar of Skippy, the peanut butter gave far too much resistance. This is not only a problem with accessibility, but with distribution. If a peanut butter is too thick, it can tear bread apart and nobody likes his or her pb&j sandwiches to be ripped up.
One last thing about Skippy is the cost. A 64 oz. jar of Skippy is about $9, while a 4lb jar of Jif peanut butter is the same cost. That is more peanut butter of a higher quality for the same cost. To me that just doesn’t make any sense. So in conclusion, If you really want a top of the line peanut butter that is just the right amount of creamy and has the classic peanut butter flavor that everyone loves, reach for Jif and you will not be disappointed.

review_title: Good sound quality, abysmal build quality.
review_text: I really enjoyed using these headphones until they failed catastrophically and fell apart. My initial review and my edit is shown below.  First impressions: These headphones are great. The sound quality is good for sub $100. For the price, I can almost give it a perfect 5 stars. The only fault I can give it is the low quality pleather pads. They do not breathe and even after short bursts I had to peel them off of my ears. In order to get these remotely wearable, you have to dump around 25 dollars on replacement pads made out of better material. Buying new pads brings the total cost of these headphones up to about 60 bucks. Are there better headphones for around 60 bucks? Maybe. It is up to you to decide to buy some DIY Panasonics or maybe drop a bit more cash on a lower end pair of Sennheisers.  Edit 8/4/15: Today one of the handles on these headphones broke, leaving one of the cups dangling off and unable to clip into place. This is on top of taping the plastic so it stays in place and doesnt pop off. This item has a very low build quality and I am upset that I had to replace them after just a few months. Seriously, do drop more on your headphones. 20 or 30 dollars extra goes a long way for buying a product that is better and long lasting out of the box.

review_title: Finally can use all six outlets
review_text:
The problem with six-outlet electrical plugs is that you rarely can use all six. Somehow, the electrical engineering wizards who design these things place the outlets way too close to each other, which basically defeats the purpose of using any appliances or electronics devices that have odd shaped adapters.

In the case of the Belkin Pivot Wall Surge Protector, the design is spot on with six outlets; each outlet can be independently swiveled. Other swivel outlets only let you swivel a bank of three at a time, which basically presents the same problem as a standard flat six-plug wall mount--you can't fit all your devices because the plugs are too close together.

This Belkin provided enough space to use every one of the outlets for my electronic gadgets. The most offending shaped one wasn't even an AC adapter, but a very large, round nightlight that hogged up two spaces. But with the Belkin Pivot, I just simply swiveled the outlet 90 degrees, and voila, problem solved.

product_name: Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System
review_title: an improvement over tv sound, but you can get better sounding equipment at this price
review_text:
I requested the Bose TV sound system hoping it would be an improvement over the cheaper Polk Audio soundbar we got a few years ago. Unfotunately, the sound isn't nearly as good on the Bose system.

We did back to back tests with tv sound, the soundbar, and the Bose system while watching music videos and a television show. The Bose system is definitely a huge improvement over the television's built-in speakers, but it doesn't come close to matching our Polk Audio soundbar. It's not surprising that our Polk Audio soundbar, which has a dedicated subwoofer would out-perform the Bose Solo system on bass, but even in the mids and highs and better on the Polk Audio system. The highs especially sound a bit tinny on the Bose system, and voices sound just a little less full on the Bose system than they are on our Polk Audio soundbar.

Comparing the Bose Solo system, which is designed to rest under a television to a soundbar that can't do that is a bit unfair. If you need a television sound system that can rest under the television so that it won't take up any extra space, the Bose Solo system is a huge improvement over standard television sound. But if you have the flexibility for another speaker configuration, there are definitely better options for your money.

product_name: Logitech Ultimate Ears 600 Noise-Isolating - Dark Silver
review_title: Great value, grab a pair while they last!
review_text:
This is my 3rd set of Logitech UEs (I had the 350's, and 500vi's prior) and the sound quality and comfort have only improved.

As a frequent traveler I can say these are perfect for flight and everywhere in between, the noise isolation works perfectly, although I can't comment on a flight longer than 9 hours. This is also the first headset that has felt reasonably secure when wearing the cord over the ear for a little stability during more active pursuits.

I'm no audiophile, so you won't catch me burning in my headphones. They serve a bit more functional purpose for me. I can't compare them to 8 other headsets on the market like some of the other reviews, but they are good enough for my needs. The sound quality for both phone and music is excellent, in my humble opinion. I am hearing things I haven't heard before in some of my 'most played song list'

The only issue, is none of the UE pairs I have purchased from Logitech have made it > 1 year before sound loss/cord fraying occurs in one ear. The loss in first pair was partly my fault, but the second I treated with kid gloves, always storing properly. While I don't really expect them to last much longer that (after doing quite a bit of review research on amazon, it seems sets 2-3x in price have the same issue), it would be nice not to have to purchase a new set each year. Something could also be said about the fact that I continue to buy them, hopefully my review doesn't lose too much credibility for that....

Anyway, for ~$50 w/prime these are a great deal. I suggest you snag a pair before they are no longer available. At this rate, I suppose next year I'll be looking at the 7 or the 900s, but who knows, maybe these will set a new longevity record!

Cheers

It's probably just a problem with the phone and not the earphones itself. They work fantastically with my laptop.  10/21/15 update: the part that connects the wire and the earphone jack; the wires inside broke apart and not the sound is weird. Really disappointed.

product_name: MidWest Poquito Avian Hotel
review_title: You might want a rubber mallet to help put this together
review_text:
I bought two of these through woot (fulfilled by Amazon) for a really good price. If it's not at a deep discount, this cage is very overpriced.

Almost every piece that has to fit together for the boltless construction on both cages was bent... either too much or too little. I had to use pliers and a rubber mallet to get the pieces together. The locks require assembly too, and most were fine, but some of the places they had to fit into were bent like crazy too. The food bowl holders were the worst.

Both of my cages also are missing a "spring" for the latch to keep the tray and grill from moving during transit. The instructions mention it but they weren't included.

Even if I assume that most of bent parts are from shipping, the top panel on one actually had a wire welded on crooked. So I'm inclined to believe that they have poor quality control in general.

Once constructed, they are pretty solid. 25 lbs solid. This will be a good cage for temporary housing such as for boarding or on vacation, as well as for going outside, but as a carrier to go to the vet, etc, I'd choose a different cage unless you want a workout. I have large flight cages that weigh less than this beast.

Overall, I was disappointed with these. I have an AA cage from before Midwest bought them and the quality between the two products is staggering.

product_name: Panasonic RP-BTGS10-A Premium Bluetooth Wireless Water-Resistant Open-Ear Headphones
review_title: Can't secure them to your head
review_text:
There's one thing I like about these, and that's that sweat won't get into them since they're designed to be sealed! Sweet! No more headseats shorting-out! However, that one awesome feature is not enough to keep me using these. Connecting via bluetooth was painless.

Issues I have are:

Battery: The battery compartment is not intuitive, you'll have to read the instructions to figure out how to charge this thing. It takes one rechargable AAA battery (included) which must be removed in order to charge, and removing it is not completely easy as there are 2 "doors" that need to be opened to get to it. Would be great if it could be charged in the headset. A USB charger is supplied for the AAA that has the ability to charge 2-AAA batteries at once, which is a nice feature.

Sound: Sound comes across as muddy. I did try to make adjustements to improve this, but was not happy with what I got. It's not terrible, but it's not great either. I guess that's the trade off for getting something that is designed to transmit through bone.

Head Straps: Included with these headphones are 2 rubber straps that go on the rear of the headset to help tighten it to your head. Only one is needed, the second one is just an extra. They are not pictured with the product but they are an essential part of it. The problem is that the way the strap is designed, it comes loose very easily and you must re-tighten/adjust the strap very frequently. This is what makes these headphones completely unacceptable for using for exercising or working out, or even sitting at the computer. The strap is a critical piece and does not perform as-needed. Also, when wearing this headset, strap or no strap, when I look up or down, the headset gets moved out of alignment and I have to readjust it. This too is unacceptable. The headset is just unable to be secured well to the head. Even sitting at my desk, the back of the headset will hit the back of my neck and get out of alignment. If the rubber strap was able to be redesigned so that it wouldn't slide off from where you set it, perhaps some of these problems would go away, but as it is, there's just no way.

Although it doesn't get rave reviews, the best exercise headset I have used has been Denon AH-W150BK Exercise Freak In-Ear Headphones. I would recommend looking at those if you need something to exercise in.

product_name: Summer Infant Metal Expansion Gate, 6 Foot Wide Walk-Thru
review_text:
I bought one of these gates a few months ago to block of a set of stairs going down to stop my then 6 month old son from falling. Needed to do some retrofitting to make it work for my situation but overall the results were great. Sturdy installation, easy open and close and easily removable. If that were my only experience with this product i would have given it 5 stars.

I just purchased another of these. I would give it one star if the first had not been so good. The screw holes on the ends of this one were not properly threaded and the bolts only go in about 3/4 to 1 inch. I decided to re-tap the holes, and quickly realized that they were a different thread count than the bolts. The door doesnt line up properly (its slightly bowed) so opening and closing requires two hands, one to open the latch and the other to bend the gate to the right position. So of my two purchases one is perfect and the other is junk. Quality control must have taken a day off. I would return it but have already been waiting a month for this to begin with and my son, now 11 months, is constantly trying to go up the stairs. At least its strong enough to stop him from doing so, its just a serious hassle for anyone else trying to get past it.

review_title: TL;DR Great quality speaker broke down 4 months in deployment
review_text:
It is with a heavy heart that the United States of Mondo has the sorrowing duty of giving you this news. On Wednesday the 8th of April 2015, there were signs of your gift Shark Boombox was not holding a charge. Many attempts were ordered to help recover Shark Boombox (or "Gomez's Shark Boombox" as he was named) including: fully depleting the current charge, charging overnight, using different cables, using different chargers, continuity testing with a multimeter, and charging off ship however it seems that all wars have casualties. Although it may not be a casualty in the common use of the word, all losses are great to those who s/he was important to.

I only knew Mondo's Shark Boombox for maybe 4 months. However it is not the amount time together that defines a relationship, but rather the quality. Boombox has a heavy unit. His solid construction gave a quiet shout of confidence that even more expensive bluetooth speakers did not have. I personally dropped Boombox a number of times as well as him flying off somewhere due to heavy seas only to brush off the dust without missing a beat.The sound quality was nice, great even. However there would be a slight loss of low end when using very bass heavy music (particularly some hip-hop). High and middle of EQ'd great.

Run time was probably Boombox's specialty. Long run times were great. Plan the night before and youll be playing music on the go out on town or just bring it along at work.The ease of use of his setup maybe all to common these days, but it is a benchmark of a nice unit. I never got to use his phone ability due to the fact that Boombox was a forward deployed speaker, however I would like to think that had I used that ability while he was in service the duties would have been followed through with great detail.

Although there will be possible others (such as : NudeAudio Super-M, Creative Sound Blaster Roar, and Photive HYDRA Rugged Water Resistant Wireless Bluetooth Speaker) I can say that the time I had with BoomBox was great although I wish he would have made the entire deployment.

V/r,
A. Gomez

product_name: DuraGear Universal Bench Seat Cover (SUV/Van), Medium Slate
review_text:
Using their measurement guide, I ordered the medium for my 2000 Explorer. I believe I would've been better off with the large. The medium fits but is so tight that it will not pull down all the way on one end and it looks nothing like the photo in as far as how smoothly it looks that it should fit. It is very obvious that it is slightly too small. It's like trying to fit a sheet on a bed that is one size too small. Plus, if you want to add seat belt availability the instructions say to CUT SLITS for them! So, I buy a new product and then have to cut holes in it? Fortunately for me, I will not be cutting slits. I bought this for intermittent use with my daughter's 100LB German Shepherd. I ordered it knowing that I was going to have to have it while I dog sat for a month and then periodically after that. I have not used it yet as the dog just got here on the day of this review. Also, there is a Velcroed slot in the middle of the cover that runs along the crease between the back of the seat and the seat itself; I assume that this is for a middle arm rest. I don't see it pictured in the advertisement. I did not have time to return the item and get a different size or a different one altogether. I probably would not buy this again. and would look at a different one.

Pros:
It seems pretty sturdy
It is not difficult to install (if the fit was better it would be even easier)
It appears that it will stay on the seat pretty well
It covers pretty well on the backside of the seat back and down along the bottom of the seat cushions
It seems like it will be easy to clean

Cons:
Size chart is not accurate, at least not for the Explorer (and I measured my seat before buying)
To use your seatbelts, you have to cut slits in your brand new item. I believe this would compromise the integrity of the material and weaken it
Due to the sizing issue mostly, this Velcroed area along the seat back and cushion pulls really tight andI am guessing that it will pull apart after a short bit of use, especially with a large dog

product_name: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_title: Great remote - using regular duracell batteries has gotten me ...
review_text:
Great remote - using regular duracell batteries has gotten me 4 months of use using the tv about 5 times a week. I'm not giving this remote 5 stars because the software to set up the remote is difficult to use for someone without tech knowledge. For example, I find it very unlikely that my father would be able to set it up on his own, and he isn't the type to be overwhelmed by PC's or smartphones. I just don't find the software accessible enough to Joe Schmo.

Despite this issue I was happy to find out the software supported my ANCIENT decade old Samsung Home Theater surround sound speaker set up. For my Verizon DVR, the only issue was finding a physical button to map the DVR list. I chose the green nondescript button in the middle of the remote, because the only other choice was a random button all the way at the bottom of the remote. Thankfully this worked out, and the rest of the buttons for the Verizon DVR were auto mapped by the dvr.

My only issue is if the phone is turned off by itself (for example it shut off because of 30 minute sleep timer), and I wish to turn it back on. I can't just press the Watch TV button a the top of the remote because this key would Turn on my TV, but turn off my home theater and cable box which remained on when my TV turned off. So to get around this, I have to enter the button set for the TV itself using the screen on the remote and press the TV On button. This can become a fairly long series of button presses (more than 3) depending on the last menu option the remote was on. Suffice to say, this can get cumbersome when all I want to do is turn the TV on.

Other than that, the IR emitter on it is plenty powerful for my small room. I've fairly satisfied.

product_name: Juicy Fruit Starburst Gum
review_title: An interesting collaboration between Juicy Fruit and Starburst, but is it worth trying?  Read on!
review_text:
For fans of Juicy Fruit and Starburst are more than likely going to enjoy the collaboration between the two brands as a new sugarfree gum featuring 15 sticks from Wrigley is now available.

I only have tried the Strawberry and the gum comes in the usual Wrigley Juicy Fruit foil paper covering. Immediately upon chewing, you can taste the Starburst.

For those that like a little long lasting flavor, unfortunately Juicy Fruit Starburst goes from Starburst to sugary sweet quite quickly, so for those wanting that long lasting Starburst taste, then you will probably want to opt for the real thing and purchase Starburst.

But I feel the collaboration of the two brands is pretty cool and it feature 35% fewer calories than sugared gum. Total carbohydrates is 1% and sugar alcohol is 2g. Total calories is 5.

Overall, I enjoyed the product for the collaboration of two solid brands. I enjoy Starburst and I enjoy Juicy Fruit...but if they could find out how to elongate that taste...I would give it perfect stars. But for now... four stars.

product_name: MEElectronics Balanced Armature In-Ear Headphones for iPod, iPhone, MP3/CD/DVD Players
review_text:
This is without a doubt the best sounding in-ear headphone for the price, or anywhere under $100 for that matter. For its price it has a very flat frequency response curve, i.e. what you hear is as close as possible to what was recorded. I have also tried the M-Duo from MEElectronics, which I suspect people who really like their bass will prefer over the A151. Personally, I prefer the A151 which delivers adequate bass without being overwhelming or making the mids and highs sound muddy.

The microphone works great even when it is hanging by the side of your head and not right next to your mouth. The remote can play/pause music on my Android phone. Comfort and sound isolation are pretty good, and also better than the M-Duo on account of the in-ear portion of the A151 being smaller. There are multiple silicon eartips to choose from, and you can where it over the ear if you want.

I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 for issues with durability. Two pairs of the first-generation A151 that I have owned have failed within a year of use; one due to a problem where the cable meets the headphone, and one due to a problem where the cable plugs into the computer/phone. The second-generation A151 has an L-shaped strain relief where the cable plugs into the computer (straight strain relief on the 1st-gen) which will probably help with durability, but the strain relief where the cable meets the headphone is unchanged. (The 2nd-gen also has a marginally better balanced armature, although I honestly can't hear the difference.) I'm not sure whether the 1st or 2nd-gen model is what's being sold by Amazon, so if you really want the 2nd-gen you might have to order directly from MEElectronics.

Another minor issue is the cable cinch on the A151P (i.e. the models with the in-line microphone). The cinch is below the microphone, so it can't really go up far enough to do its job. (Or maybe my head is just the wrong size.) The combination of the cinch andin-line microphone also seem to make the cable more susceptible to tangling. Again, only a minor issue unless you plan to take these headphones along for your workout.

review_title: Great design, meets the mark for many of the classic Sony headphone merits
review_text: UPDATE:  After the original unit malfunctioned (read original story below if interested), I received a free replacement and they have functioned perfectly for almost a month thus far. I don't have any reason to suspect these will stop working prematurely. It did seem the first unit I received was an aberration, and in any case it was easy to get it replaced with a working unit.  My updated impression of these headphones is they are ideal in most respects: they are light, stick well in the ears, have the conventional over-head headband design, etc. The only real downside is that when compared to the cheaper price of the old Sony models (often between $8-16) they don't feel as "disposable" and thus I'm a little for paranoid about things happening to them. Still, if they last for several months (let's hope!) they are easily worth the $25 for any runners who are attached to this style of headphone.  ORIGINAL REVIEW:  I was excited about these headphones because, like many others, I perceived them to fill the void left by Sony's various "sport" headphones which have been discontinued. The first day or two using these for running had me excited to report that they were indeed everything that I'd been hoping for. So many of the nuances are right: good fit, decent sound, long cord, appropriate flex in the headband. It's a great design in many respects.  I'm torn about how to review the product because unfortunately, after less than two weeks of use the audio cut out on one earphone. I'm used to this, as I'm sure any runner is: after months of use under running conditions, headphones inevitably break down like this. Even with the utmost care the jostling of the cables eventually leads to a shorted out wire or something else that spells the end, then you suck it up and buy another pair.  But I can't suck it up and buy another pair after two weeks.  To be completely fair I'm going to buy one more pair and hope for the best that this was an aberration. I see some other reviews alluding to short life expectancy so I don't know if there is a systematic problem or if some of us are just bound to get unlucky. If I have a better experience with the new pair I will update this review, but I want to put the problem out there so other folks who may experience it can corroborate the experience.  Update April 6, 2015 11PMEST: I think it's worth noting that within a day of writing this review I had a response from the sellers (see below) politely explaining a possible cause for the defective behavior, and offering to refund the purchase (which I have now seen come through via Amazon). There's an obviously negative angle to my review above, but I hope it also comes through that I want the product to be great. Hopefully I will find that my first experience was an aberration, and will definitely update the review and star rating if so.  In any case I would like to commend the particular sellers for being on top of their feedback and proactively seeking to remedy things.

product_name: House of Marley Uplift Midnight In-Ear Headphones
review_title: These House of Marley headphones are good, not great
review_text:
These House of Marley headphones are good, not great. I’ll get the major drawback out of the way first. Because of the braided fabric cord, the microphonics (you know that loud sound you get when the cord rubs against your shirt or jacket?) are TERRIBLE. These have to be the worst pair of headphones I’ve had in this respect although, to be fair, this is my first pair ever with a fabric-covered cord. My previous pairs (MEElectronics M9P, Apple, some other random Panasonics, Sonys, and others – none particularly HIGH quality) have been better than the Marleys. If you jog with these, forget about a clean sound.

Also, the cords are not as tangle-free as others. Better than some, but not as good as others. They still tangle, in my experience.

On the positive side, they do have a very distinctive look, if that’s your thing. I don’t mind them. The sound is also pretty good, if a bit bass-heavy. My pair has a mic with a single button (mutes when on a call, pauses/plays music) which works on my Android phone. Sound quality is acceptable, I’m told, although you pretty much do have to hold the mic up to your mouth and shield any kind of wind – mic is average. They also seem fairly durable in the 5-6 months I’ve had them, given that I travel frequently and use them every trip (I do have a pair of Bose QC25’s I use when on the plane, but tend to use the Marleys otherwise).

In all, I think there are better options out there (the MEElectronics M9P, for example, I would recommend over these for the price, or the Sennheiser MM30), but these are a decent set and would have rated better, were it not for the microphonics.

review_text: I decided to try this product based on a bunch of positive reviews and the fact that almond butter tends to be super expensive in groceries and health food stores. I am definitely disappointed after trying this out several times. The first thing I noticed was that the consistency was a bit weird - much stiffer than normal almond butter. It's almost like when you have regular almond butter on the sides of the jar that tends to dry out a little and it becomes more chunky - except I found the whole jar to be like that. It's difficult to spread and since I like to eat my almond butter with slices of apples, I ended up slapping a big unsightly chunk on there and having to take small bites from it as I make my way through the apple slice. The flavour was also disappointing - I figured it would taste similar to any roasted almond butter, however when I received the jar I noticed the ingredients list states "blanched roasted almonds". Not sure if that's why, but it definitely has a bland taste. If I want a sugar-free product I would be more satisfied with a raw almond butter that is literally just raw almonds. It's much tastier and smoother. I guess almond butter is a little more expensive for a reason - I would personally rather pay more for a product that I will enjoy.

Old review:

This is going to be a two pronged review focusing on the batteries and then the travel charger.

These SecurityIng 18650 Li-Ion Rechargeable Batteries have been working well in the lights (tactical style LED torches) that we have been trying them in today. Those lights have low to moderate draw, and are acceptable use for these style batteries. I would recommend these batteries to others for such use, based on our experience, though would like more information on the source battery used and the specifics of the drain and overcharge protection. For the sale price (currently under ten bucks for the entire set), the batteries have worked quite well.

The travel charger that came with these batteries truly seems underpowered or over constrained. After plugging in the travel charger for our test, putting it and the batteries in a fire proof soft case, and heading out to lunch... we returned two hours later to find them not yet charged.

After another couple hours, they had enough charge to work but were still not fully charged. I used Nitecore Intelligent i4 Charger (version 2) to finish the job, and once the batteries were properly charged they lit up the light well.

So here is my quandary: Inexpensive 18650 batteries that do the job when charged in a quality charger, five stars, delivered with a travel charger that just does not get the job done, one star. Since it really is the batteries that we care about, I blended those ratings into four overall stars.

The Amazon listing notes that these batteries are covered by a \\"30 Days Money Back Guarantee\\" and a \\"12 Months Warranty\\", so if an issue occurs within those periods I will return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. I am not going to bother replacing the travel charger since we have other options. We did receive these batteries gratis from the seller and put them to use to objectively find out how well they performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

If you are looking for 18650 batteries of this style, capacity, price and size, and if you are familiar with the properties and risk of these types of batteries and take appropriate precautions when using and charging, then these SecurityIng 18650 batteries might be just the batteries that you are looking for... but maybe you should consider other charger options like we did.

review_title: NOT RECOMMENDED: Horrible song management, confusing hardware layout, unintuitive and ununiformed controls, and more
review_text:
I originally wasn’t going to review the Tom America MP3 Player. Though, it’s so bad, that I felt an injustice by ignoring it. This is what you’d buy from Chinatown as a Christmas gag gift. If it isn’t a gag gift, you’ll either use it once before it breaks, or break it yourself. Details inside, including a full TLDR.

▶ Package Contents
• Tom America MP3 Player
• 16gb Micro SD Card
• Mini USB Cable
• 3.5mm Stereo Earphones
• User manual

▶ Specifications
Usually I’d state specifications here, but this MP3 player has absolutely no documentation for such information.

▶ Hardware
The hardware of the Tom America MP3 Player is very confusing. It tries very hard to be an iPod Nano clone, but fails miserably.

It measures at 3.75” x 1.6” x 0.25” with a 2” LCD screen. As the iPod Nano, at the bottom features a “mouse wheel”, which really is four buttons: Menu, Volume, Next Track, and Previous Track. At the center of the mouse wheel is an ON/OFF/Back/(Other?) button, but I’ve noticed that the switch at the top controls ON/OFF as well.

What seems as a trivial pursuit in hardware is even worse in software.

Picture this. You turn on the media player and are welcomed by a wonderful multi-color display. The display is very much pixelated, but pictures and video are easily recognizable. It’s nothing to complain about at its price point.

I’ve been trying very hard to objectively use this MP3 player for the past few days. Unfortunately, it has become very difficult to use an MP3 Player with lackluster buttons. I’ve literally had to hard press the buttons in order for them to work. I’ve never had to apply such force to an MP3 player before.

This made playing games almost impossible. It’s difficult to play Tetris or Snake when the feedback of the buttons are over a second long.

review_title: High end product if that's what you want, or need.
review_text:
Be aware with this series of plugs that wires are not held in with set screws. They are fed through a tube and the stripped portion of the wire doubled back over the tube and held in place when the end cap is screwed on. Not a very good description, but I don't know how else to describe it.

With this design, they will work best with 12 gauge wire, or maybe 14. Smaller gauge wire will not fit snugly enough to work as well. Although it may fit, a cheaper series would probably function better.

The plugs are also rather wide. So if space is a consideration, you might want to consider a different series or brand.

I bought these because they were on sale. Otherwise I would have bought something cheaper. After all, the main requirement is just to get good contact at the end of a speaker wire. If you're using quality heavy gauge wire these would be a good fit. If you're using cheapo 18 gauge, it's like putting $300 Pirellis on a Yugo.

product_name: Farm-fresh: 100% Kona Coffee, Medium Roast, Whole Beans, 1 Lb
review_title: Inconsistent coffee - sometimes good, sometimes awful
review_text:
When you get a good bag of Blue Horse kona, it's really good coffee. Unfortunately, I don't feel I can count on it to be consistently good. I've purchased it twice now, and the first time it was heavenly. However, the second purchase was a totally different experience. The first couple pots from the bag were fine, nothing special. But after that, the beans lost their aroma, the coffee started tasting sour, and I have had to throw the rest away. An expensive few cups of coffee!

I stored the coffee and prepared it exactly the same way as before. I have no idea what may have happened. Perhaps the beans were exposed to extraordinary heat during the shipping, causing them to spoil. I don't know.

I emailed Blue Horse to let them know of this experience, and while they were apologetic that it happened, they couldn't offer any explanation, nor did they offer a replacement or refund.

It pains me to write this review. I had been so excited and looking forward to enjoying this coffee as my weekend treat. The cost means it's not something I can do for myself but a few times a year. I won't be purchasing from Blue Horse again because I simply can't afford to throw away $36.

product_name: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)
review_title: Enjoyable, but leaves me wanting more
review_text:
I've had this device for a few months now, and have had my eyes on other reviews to see what others think of it. I'm ready to join the fray.
-Sounds quality: I'm pretty happy overall, coming from an iPod Classic, I notice a bump in quality. This perceived difference is certainly impacted by the type of music and quality of recording. Jazz, electronic, and certain types of rock sound pretty great. Most of my music is either MP3, AAC, or ALAC, and all are handled well. Sound is the recent I got this, and for the price, it has delivered.
-Hardware: Nice slim form, easy controls I can use without looking at them. Screen is plenty big and lack of touchscreen is not missed at all. Scrolling through lots of songs/artists can be a bit tedious with only directional keys, but not terribly onerous. A big negative here though, and something I don't see often from Sony- poor build quality on the SIM card slot (which I've seen mentioned elsewhere): the door barely stays closed and is not flush. Not a deal breaker, but annoying. Worse, is a slight opening in the casing along the side with the volume buttons. Sure, I've probably dropped this thing a few times by now, but a couple of feet off the ground, not off a building. I'm not concerned, but my old iPod was a solid as a rock (not to mention totally seamless).
-Device software: Basic and functional. Options to look at photos and watch videos, and frankly, I don't think it's necessary. It's easy to access playlists, the music I'm looking for, shuffle, and equalizer settings. It's not as sexy as the iPod software, but it does the job.
-Computer/media transfer software: I have a Mac, and should note that Sony did put out an updated transfer software release (Content Transfer version 1.1.11140) that solved many issues from transferring music and playlists from iTunes. By dragging and dropping, it is easy to move songs (and the artwork goes along with it). The strange part is the playlist- if you transfer a playlist, it doesn't just move over the info of what songs to play, it moves over all the songs (again). So, if you make a new playlist in iTunes, then drag it over to the Walkman, it will attempt to move each and every song over (and, again and again, realize the file is already there and move to the next). This takes forever for what amounts to a text file.

-Memory: Major pros/cons here. The 64 GB on board storage is a good start. But, with lossless files, fills up quick. I purchased a 128 GB micro SIM card to max it out. The device can seamless play files from either storage location, but putting them on there requires careful planning- once one fills up, don't expect the software to know to start moving files to the other location. Still, the 192 total capacity is great with flexibility to put files on other cards.

Overall: I feel like most of my points were negative, but I generally like using this Walkman. I think it could use some fine tuning: software, transfer software especially. Ideally, I'd love to see Sony find a way to make a plug-in for iTunes so I can interface directly (not sure how Apple would feel about it, but worth dreaming about). iPods were famously easy to use, and should be the benchmark for any portable audio device. If you are looking for something that will sound better than your smart phone, this is a great place to start.

product_name: Timex T231W2 AM/FM Dual Alarm Clock Radio with 1.2-Inch Green Display and Line-In Jack (White)
review_title: Simple solutions to common complaints about this clock.
review_text: I bought this clock about a week ago. Several reviewers have mentioned that the display on this clock is too bright, even when the display dimmer is used. Personally, I don't think the dimmed display is all that bright. Dimmed display or not, I have discovered a simple solution to this problem: CLOSE YOUR EYES. The nice thing is, I no longer use my bedroom nightlight for the times I have to get up to answer nature's call. My nightlight was brighter, but this clock casts an adequate glow on the ceiling. Saves me a tiny bit of electricity by unplugging the nightlight. The OTHER problem mentioned by reviewers is that, with the exception of the "snooze" bar, the REST of the control buttons are all the same size, and very small, and so are hard to distinguish one from another, especially when you are trying to operate the alarm functions in the dark. The control button design IS poor, and you shouldn't have to do what I did, but it works, and for the price of this otherwise decent clock, it was worth the effort. I simply purchased a pack of those little rubber-like, self-adhesive, pea-sized, cushioning beads (available at Wal-Mart, Target, hobby stores, etc.) and stuck one bead to each of the 2 alarm buttons. Voila! NOW I can feel the alarm buttons in the dark without wondering what function I am about to change, and with the 2 now-easy-to-feel alarm buttons as "home base," in the dark I simply count buttons to whichever other function I want to operate. Works perfectly. I suggest wiping the alarm buttons with a little rubbing alcohol first, to help the beads to stick better. Other than this, I am very happy with this clock. And, really, the big, bright display makes it easy to see the time when your eyes are clogged with sleepiness in the middle of the night.

product_name: SOL Republic Unisex Shadow Wireless In-Ear Headphones
review_title: Excellent sound and value for the price!
review_text: I purchased these at Best Buy since I didn't want to wait to get via delivery, but the price is the same as Amazon, so for those who are ordering, I wanted to give you a review. I have tried many earbuds, from inexpensive to extremely expensive and right now my favorite wired earbuds are the RHA T10's which run $185 here at Amazon and $200+ elsewhere. I needed a pair of bluetooth wireless that had good sound and tried many from $150 to $300. On a whim, I went and purchased these at Best Buy and tried them in the parking lot. Wow! These are the first wireless earbuds that match the sonic quality of the RHA's. The highs are crisp and clean with nice thumping bass that are not over exaggerated. The mid-tones are a little too flat, but for $99 these are no-brainers. Ed Sheeran's X sounds crisp and clean you can hear him sliding his fingers across the guitar. Next up was Al Green's Let's Stay Together, Yeah! Green's velvety voice comes through without blending into the arrangement. The horns are crystal clear and the bass is not over powering. Okay, how about some jazz. John Coltrane's Blue Train came through with all it's power. Coltrane's saxophone takes center stage with no clipping at the high notes. Ummm...yeah. Paul Chamber's bass is ever present in the background and Lee Morgan's trumpet comes through without competing with Coltrane. Now let's really test them, Green Day's American Idiot. Yowzah! These babies crank! The separation in this stereo recording is fantastic and the Sol Republics reproduce them without any issues. The power of the track comes through without any problem with a tight bass throughout. Okay, these passed the test for me. Are they perfect? No, I don't think any set of earbuds or cans are, but for $99? I don't think you can get better sound than these for that price point. Unlike others have said, I don't have any problem with the design of these in-ear headphones. They're comfortable and the band feels comfortable around my neck. If you are looking for clean sound regardless of being wireless, check out the RHA 10T's, but if you need wireless and want to save some bucks, don't hesitate, buy these puppies. review_text:
Very nice while they are working. I received a pair from my wife for my birthday and was thrilled with the performance and comfort. When you pay $300 for earbuds - you expect quality and durability - Bose quiet comfort 20 acoustic noise cancelling earbuds miss the mark on durability.

product_name: StarTech.com HDMI Over Dual CAT5 / CAT6 Extender with Infrared IR 100ft /30m HDMI Over Ethernet Cable Extender Power Free 1080p
review_title: It works well, IF your HDMI port supplies enough voltage to the unit
review_text:
Ok, here is the deal with this device. It's a passive device, meaning it does not have a power supply that plugs into it, it uses PoE or power over ethernet, in this case, power over HDMI. This was the feature that was so attractive to me for this device because I do not have utility power at the receiver point in my blu-ray to projector setup. So the transmitter unit relies completely on the power it gets from the HDMI port of your device. IF your device (blu-ray, computer, game system) does not provide sufficient current to the transmitter unit from the HDMI port, it can not stay connected whether you run 28m or 3m of cable. This was the case for me. I would plug the device in and it would flash the display for a moment and then go away. The lights on the StarTech would just blink. I must have re-crimped my CAT 6 connectors 4 or 5 times before I just got frustrated.

I had set up an return authorization with AV House to return the device but decided to give it one last try, so I went over to RadioShack and bought a $20 powered HDMI in line amplifier, key word being powered. This little bugger has a 5VDC/1A power supply that ramps up the power of the HDMI signal and when I plugged that in front of my StarTech transmitter, the signal locked in and I had a very solid transmission that has streamed without lag, skip, or fail to this point.

My advice, would be to buy a powered unit to avoid the hours of frustration I had to deal with, but if you can't supply utitlity power to the receiver end of your extender then this device is a better option. Just be prepared to potentially drop another few bucks on a powered amplifier if your device can't support it.

review_title: Just didn't live up to expectations
review_text:
The waterproof feature of the speaker is top-notch, and it has survived several trips to the pool, where my kids promptly put it into heavy use by taking it into the water. It then became a bit of a toy as they threw it back and forth to each other. This hasn't affected the performance or functionality of the speaker one bit. A single charge also lasts longer than we would need it to for a daily outing, and connecting multiple phones to it via Bluetooth was no problem whatsoever.

That said...

I just don't like it as much as it's non-waterproof brother (The NYNE Portable Bluetooth Speaker: http://www.amazon.com/NYNE-Multimedia-Inc-Portable-Bluetooth/dp/B00I9ID070/ref=sr_1_8?ie=UTF8&qid=1429031820&sr=8-8&keywords=nyne+speaker). I understand the waterproof aspect of the speaker has a detrimental effect on the sound (even out of water), but I'm a total baby about how speakers perform. This speaker sounds tinny, and has very little bass response. Bluetooth speakers in general don't always have the best performance, but there are a few on the market - including the NYNE speaker I linked to above - that provide substantially better sound.

If you're needing a speaker you can totally abuse for your outings to the pool, lake, etc, and you don't really care too much about the sound, then this should definitely be your go-to. However, if you're an audio baby like I am, I would recommend going with it's big brother I linked above.

review_title: I so wanted to keep these!
review_text:
These headphones are a good value for what they are, but they have a few flaws and one that is a deal killer for me.

Pros:
+ They have good sound for the money. They are muddy out of the box, but can be tuned with a good equalizer.
+ They have the best control system I have every run across. Very simple and intuitive. I wish all headphones used this control scheme.
+ They look cool! Subjective I know, but I like them.
+ They pair easily and just work.

Cons:

review_text:
Ok...this whole system is pretty good so far. In one opening, which was about 6 or 7 feet I am no longer in that house and have forgotten the exact measurements) I used one 14 inch extension and one 39 inch extension with the gate. The extensions go together easily and appear to be very sturdy. The gate opens easily.
The only difficulty I had was in the actual size of the extensions WITH THE WALL ATTACHMENTS. Be careful when you measure because the wall attachments take up an additional 1-2 inches on each end of the whole structure. I was able to use only the glue attachments for the first area where I placed the gate setup because there really was no room to set the more permanent screw in wall attachments.
With the second doorway opening I had to return one of the 14 inch attachments and exchange it for the 10 inch attachment because of the aforementioned problem. Also...make sure you do NOT have the quarter round molding on the bottom of the wall because the structure necessitates direct contact with the floor all the way across its width...You can have molding, but it must be flat, not quarter round. So, in the second opening I had to remove the quarter round molding cut out an area for the gate attachment and replace it.
The whole structure is actually attractive so no worries about that.

product_name: Klipsch Reference On-Ear Premium Headphone
review_text:
These headphones are superb quality in all aspects. The packaging, the fit and finish, and most importantly the audio performance are all excellent. I am extremely happy with these headphones second only to my Bose QC15.

This is my first pair of on-ear headphones, I have always preferred the over the ear style. I find that the foam on these ear-pieces is very comfortable for long periods of time. The foam is compliant enough to allow the ear pieces to block out some of the ambient noise. Most importantly they don't pinch my ears into my glasses as bad as my other pairs allowing me to listen for longer periods of time.

These headphones deliver exceptional dynamic range allowing me to hear subtleties in songs I know well, but just never heard with other headphones. I have been unable to hear any distortion with the maximum volume an I-phone or Dell PC can deliver. More importantly I don't feel that I need to crank these up to hear the details.

The cord is a flat ribbon which is a good length if you are plugged into a device you are carrying with you but a bit short for sitting at a desk plugged into a stationary computer. I really wish the cable had connectors at both ends so it could be replaced if damaged, but that isn't the case. The cable end is a very small diameter so it should work with all phone or tablet protective cases. The cable is a 4 contact style and has worked fine with most devices with conventional 3 contact connectors, but sound was garbled with 1 adapter that I had until I pulled the cable out of the connector slightly.

There is a microphone on the cable near the top and it has 3 buttons on it. The center button will pause and play Pandora if that app is running, otherwise holding it brought up Siri (I-phone). The top and bottom buttons are volume control on the phone. Having a phone conversation using these headphones and microphone is as clear as can be.

My only criticism of this product are the flat cable which is not replaceable and seems like it would be prone to kink. The other issue is a weird interaction between my ears and the on-ear design which causes me to hear high frequency more clearly if I move my jaw a certain way. product_name: Aune T1 MK2 (Second Generation) 6922 24bit/192kHz Tube Amplifier Mini Hi-fi USB DAC Decoder "Fashion Black"
review_text: I recently received this DAC and headphone amp to upgrade my Topping D1 Mark 2 DAC. I must say the Aune T1 MK2 is amazing and the extra cost over the Topping DAC is well worth it. Last night I listened for hours and heard detail I had never before heard before, and the imaging was fantastic. I listen with a pair of Shure SRH440 headphones and am using the 6922EH tube supplied with the DAC.  (I have a Gold Lion on order).  While the DAC used in the Aune is capable of 192KHz, the USB front-end is limited to 96KHz. The tube is used in the DAC stage, not the headphone amplification stage.  As others have mentioned, the Aune is heavy. It is beautifully made and solid. My only complaint is about the plastic cover over the tube. I had to file it down on the bottom in order for it to fit and I broke one of them (fortunately they send two of them which might not be enough if you swap out tubes). The +/- 15v power supply is heavy as well. The large volume control is smooth, but I recommend starting out with it turned way down since this is not an iPod and should have the power to drive any headphone.  When you power it on it will remain mute for 30 seconds to give the tube time to warm up before a white LED under the tube lights up, a nice effect.  Almost all of the music I played was in FLAC format, ripped directly from my CDs although one piece I bought in FLAC format, 176Khz, 24-bit.  My laptop is running OpenSUSE Linux and I used Amarok to play my music. Linux recognized the USB audio device which required no special configuration.  I played a lot of Pink Floyd including the Endless River and David Gilmore's Live in Gdansk (MP3). The sound was more detailed than I remember and very musical.  I then played Escala, however I found listening to this album was difficult. It sounded muddy and distorted and actually harsh. In order to see if it was the DAC or the recording I next played the Sheffield Track and Drum Record (CD FLAC).  When I played the Sheffield Track and Drum record I heard a lot more detail than I had ever heard before, especially in the percussion. The soundstage was absolutely amazing where I could exactly place every percussion hit and every note. I want to say that it sounded very technical and exact, not overly warm but extremely detailed. It may even be just a bit bright, but that may also just be my headphones which I'll admit aren't the best ones out there.  I next listened to a recording of Stravinsky's The Firebird Suite (1919) (FLAC) which was recorded at 176KHz, 24-bit. The FLAC files retain the original 24-bit, 176KHz recording. This was amazing. I could place every instrument in the orchestra and hear detail I had never before heard. It was an amazing experience.  Compared to the Topping T1 Mark 2 the Aune sounds much more detailed and richer and the bass is much stronger. The Topping T1 also has a problem when a cell phone is nearby in that the signal gets amplified from the headphone cord. I had to place ferrite beads over my headphone cable as well as the USB cable. Topping could easily fix the problem by putting some RF filtering in their op-amp stage. I found no such problem with the Aune T1.  I will update this after I receive the other tubes I have on order.  Update: I got the Gold Lion tube and am pleased to say that it only improved the sound. The detail is still crystal clear but it doesn't sound quite as bright and more musical with a nice tonal quality to it. I have figured out how to better tune the audio subsystem in Linux which sucks with its default settings.  The default Linux ALSA and Pulse Audio settings leave a lot to be desired. The following changes will significantly improve the audio quality:  Add the following two lines:  defaults.pcm.dmix.rate 96000 defaults.pcm.rate_converter speexrate_best  to ~/.asoundrc  Copy /etc/pulse/daemon.conf to ~/.config/pulse/daemon.conf and change or add the following lines:  resample-method = src-sinc-best-quality default-sample-format = s24le default-sample-rate = 96000  This change significantly improves the sample rate conversion quality and allows it to output and mix at 96KHz.  Update 2: One thing I really love about this DAC is the fantastic imaging. When listening to a Reference Recordings 24-bit 176 KHz FLAC recording I have of Stravinsky's Firebird Suite I can place each instrument on the sound stage. It's not just simple left, center, right but far more detailed. When I close my eyes I can place each instrument playing in the orchestra. As a test I played the Sheffield Track and Drum record recording (ripped from CD to FLAC). The detail was simply amazing. When listening to the percussion parts I could easily place where each hit was struck, even the soft background ticks. When Jim Keltner is brushing the drums you can hear which direction the brush is moving, the imaging is simply amazing as is the detail. I heard a lot of things I had previously missed, such as the soft background ticks which I had never noticed before with my Topping headphone DAC.  The tube warmth is certainly there though I would not consider it to be strong or adding significant coloration to the sound.  So far my only real complaint is that the plastic pieces that go over the tube are quite delicate. When transporting it I managed to break one of the tabs on the bottom of my second set. I also had to file the tabs down in order for them to fit.  While the T1 MK2 is fairly immune to interference caused by a nearby cell phone it is not completely immune. Adding a ferrite bead with one wrap of the headphone cord seems to have completely eliminated the problem. My Topping T1 MK2 DAC on the other hand was far more sensitive.

product_name: Summer Chiffon Ruffle Neck Sleeveless Evening Ball Gown Long Maxi Dress
review_title: Exactly what I was looking for!
review_text:
At 37 weeks pregnant and the heaviest I've been in my life I'm about to attend my stepdaughters wedding this upcoming weekend. I've been looking for a maxi dress that will fit me, look gorgeous but not break the bank. Who wants to purchase a formal maternity dress? The answer is no one because it will never be worn again.

Anyway, after reading reviews I decided to order this dress as a back up, just in case the other one I ordered didn't look good on me. I figured if it didn't fit I'll just return it. Turns out it fits me with room to spare, it looks gorgeous and I'm thinking I'll end up returning the other dress (an actual maternity dress) because this one is my favorite. Even when I lose the pregnancy weight I'll still be able to wear this dress because I can tell it will also look great on a smaller body type/non-pregnant woman.

A few things: 1) the neck hole is sort of big but not so big that it looks ridiculous or anything, 2) the clasps at the neck aren't sewn on securely so make sure you secure them yourself once you get the dress, 3) it is sort of see-through but nothing a slip can't correct, and 4) even though I'm 5'7'' with a giant pregnant belly this dress comes down to my ankles--not a problem for me but I imagine a much shorter woman would have a problem with the length.

Also, the dress is true to the color shown in the picture, in case anyone was wondering.

review_text:
This is my second Harmony remote and they have both worked well with certain limitations. The old remote, a 10 yr old similar model was showing wear and tear such as sticky keys, otherwise was still working. The new 650 is just slightly better than the old. For one, online setup was even easier than before with about as simple a walk through initial setup as you could want. Also, the new Harmony solved a TV input selection problem that old remote could not solve even with tech support help. If your setup is very basic then the Harmony will work perfectly. If you have some complexities then there will be some setup work to do. In my case my TIVO took some customizing before I got it work mostly right. I really do not fault the remote for this trial-and-error necessity, I'm just asking it do some complex commands. Since the online customizing menu is easy to use it's kind of fun playing around changing the commands.
Overall, the remote does about 90% of what I need, about a 4.5 star review.

review_title: I don't know why I waited so long...
