product_name: Denon DBT-1713UD 3D Ready Blu-ray disc, DVD, Super Audio CD Player with Networking
review_title: Suffers from serious technical flaws and high cost
review_text:
I've been a long time Denon fan, but unfortunately, the DBT-1713UD shows that Denon is a mere shadow of its former self. I first purchased this unit as a refurb, and it was a dud right out of the box. Ok, it happens, right? So, I return it to Denon directly who, after several weeks of me requesting status, decided to send me a brand new unit.

Thinking that was the end of my trouble, I soon realized that Denon is out of its depth when dealing with streaming. I purchased this unit to replace it's adequate but painfully slow predecessor, the DBP-1610, because I wanted a unit that offered streaming capability as well. The performance of this unit is somewhat faster when handling blu-rays, and that's about the extent of its benefits.

The firmware in this device is horrible; even after a few updates, it is not production quality. The streaming mode, whenever the streaming menu is shown, is a dedicated mode and must be exited using the remote before even trying to eject the tray to put a disc in. The buttons on the unit are unresponsive until you exit this mode.

The interaction between the device firmware and the built-in Netflix app is ridiculous. To register the device, the netflix username and password must be entered using an onscreen keyboard. Much more inconvenient than entering a device code from the Netflix website like many other players use. This is especially frustrating when the player will "forget" my credentials after a few failed attempts when trying to stream. Half the time when I select a title to play, the player drops out of the netflix app. I must re-enter the streaming menu, select the netflix app and start again. Every so often, after a few of these dropouts, my credentials are gone and I need to re-enter them... on that !@#$@! on screen keyboard.

The Hulu app seems much more stable, but the navigation for it is not intuitive compared to the browser version. The youtube app is probablythe best of the bunch, as it seems the most stable and the easiest to navigate.

I would say 1 out of 8 discs I initially insert cause the player to freeze and become unresponsive while it tries to access it, this is especially true if the player has already been in a streaming session. It requires that I power cycle the machine, and then it begins playing the disc normally. This is with BD-Live disabled, of course, which I did first thing. The BD-Live functionality I found is much more trouble than its worth and slows down disc interaction quite a bit.

Other manufacturers are providing the same level of video and audio performance, coupled with much more capable firmware features for, in many case, a fraction of the cost of what Denon is offering. It pains me to say that this will be my last Denon product.

review_text:
Anxiously waiting for the UPS man,
I finally destroy box that's as tall as a child.
Banana plugs, AV receiver, TV, meet Klipsch KF-26 Icon.
Movies feel like I am right there at the theater.
Music has life and it's like I'm sipping a beer at a concert.
Playing Madden NFL 15 on Xbox One felt like I was in the game.
Just these two speakers rattled my socks off.
Everything audio with these just has life, power, and precision.

Some thoughts on setup and audio performance:
While this pair is good enough as it is, getting the KC-25 Icon center speaker would top it all of. I don't think the KF-28 is necessary, unless you've got some serious cash saved up or the audio heaven fund to support it. These two speakers could (though I wouldn't) bring down the house. At 30 watts, there is some rumbling. The subwoofer (there are some built into the KF-26 already) not needed, but again, always a plus. 100 Watts on BOTH speakers? Woo! Make sure the home av receiver can support the 100 watts per channel. My Sony 7.1 AV receiver connects flawlessly. I used banana plugs (don't judge me) hooked between these speakers and the AV receiver. Clear, no buzzing, just audio pindrop perfection.

Design -
Wow. The wood feels and looks beautiful. The black will look good with any furniture or room. Without the grill, your guests can really admire the tweeters and built in subwoofer. The grill looks good on the speaker and is easy to pop off. The connection module is located on the back of the speaker, roughly a bit lower than the bottom half. I hope this helps other RVers and campers when they hit their home sites.

product_name: Panasonic Clip Headphones Blue
review_text:
I decided to try these after my pair of Sony Clip ones broke (The Sony ones I had: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000MX7Z3K?refRID=HT8PEBCJ23ZXCMQYQKJ2&ref_=pd_rhf_cr_p_img_9 The broke because something chewed through the wire ^^; so it wasn't the headphones fault.). So My review of these is based in did I like these better than those.

Sound: While I don't have my old Sony ones to do a direct comparison with I would say the sound on these is definitely more clear in comparison. That said I don't think these head phones are very good for music. There is like 0 bass. Which isn't necessarily a problem since i got them for play games with, and I tested them out with a Drama CD and I think the voice was definitely more clear. I even compared them with the headphones that came with my Samsung galaxy phone and I'd still say they are better for just straight vocals. The earbuds that came with the phone gave a sort of tin can like tint to the audio in comparison to these. These aren't bad but they aren't great.

Comfort: I found these less comfortable than my old Sony ones. The clip on is weird. Instead of retracting it lifts up. I don't find it comfortable and they don't feel as secure because of it. I think it makes the speaker not close enough to the ear. Like when I press down on the speaker the audio get's better. I also feel like the speaker is a tad bit too big and covers too much space as my ears started getting hot while wearing them for under 5 minutes.

Conclusion: For the price they aren't bad if you play game or listen to audio books, but I'm still chasing after a pair of clips that can compare to the discontinued Sony ones I really liked.

product_name: KID INSPIRED Bluetooth Speaker Cube with LED Lights JOMBY® JUKEBOX Black
review_title: ... this speaker is very well done and it looks great (save for the random sticker in the corner that ...
review_text: The design of this speaker is very well done and it looks great (save for the random sticker in the corner that says the product title "Jomby Jukebox". The lights work well and I do like how the buttons are discreet (you press it on top and it actually pushes the cube down to push the button on the bottom of the box). So why am I giving it two stars? Whenever you turn on this speaker, it has the absolute most loud and obnoxious opening dubstep sequence with a strange distorted voiceover (It sounds like it's saying "this is your iPhone 4 speaking") and then immediately followed by a voiceover saying the bluetooth is on, however it's not a pleasant voiceover like Siri or Google, it sounds like a direct recording of someone's voice, however it doesn't seem like English is their native tongue. When the bluetooth connects the same person speaks again, and they're actually a bit difficult to understand because of their accent. I would much prefer a "beep" in confirmation, and no sound at all when it turns on. While I do feel the pricetag of 25$ is definitely reasonable considering this box can get rather loud for it's size, music quality is okay, and the lights are cool, I really can't get over the awkward voiceover and having to listen to the weird 15 second dubstep opening everytime I turn it on. I haven't had this product for long, so I can't attest for it's durability over time, but it's decent--- and if you dont mind the opening sequence and voiceover, it's definitely worth the money. I previously owned the Mobi Cube and bought this to replace it since my Cube died due to the common problem of the Cube refusing to charge after a few months. I prefer the lights and design of the Jomby Jukebox, but the Mobi Cube had a better build quality, adjustable light functions, much better sound quality, and most importantly, no dubstep, no voiceover.

As soon as I turned on the bluetooth on my phone, it found the speaker. I pressed "Pair" and it was ready to go.  The sound quality is crisp, clear, and plays at a decent volume in smaller spaces. In my bedroom, I thought the volume was loud enough to hear, but I did need to keep it turned to its loudest setting to get the full experience. While the bluetooth was paired with my phone, I was even able to accept a call, just by answering with the speaker's "call" button and talking into it. That was such a bonus feature to this device!  Now, because of its compact size, the volume projected from the speakers is medium, but not able to fill a large room. Outside of my house, the surrounding noise overwhelmed the sound coming from the device. I also found it a little tedious to hold the rewind/forward button to increase and decrease the volume. I would have preferred a separate volume button.  Watch my demonstration: http://youtu.be/xiMrINYE0WQ  The DKnight MagicBox Wireless Speaker is a great portable bluetooth speaker to use to project music from your phone. It's not super loud, but I don't expect any of the compact speakers to go beyond a certain volume. It still has a clear and exceptional sound quality with good playback time. And of course it's ultra portable and user-friendly.  *Disclosure: I received this product free from the company in exchange for my honest opinion and review.

product_name: EZCAP.TV 116 EzGrabber USB 2.0 Video Capture VHS to DVD Converter for Windows Vista/7/8/10 Mac OSX 10.5.8
review_title: Steps for Audio Fix and Copyprotection Fix - Windows 7 - Ezcap now works perfectly for me!
review_text:
This product DOES work with my Windows 7. I had problems at the beginning getting it installed correctly, because the company doesn't put the correct drivers on the disc, as many others have also stated. I found this solution WORKS, from another reviewer with Windows 7:
1.Plug the ezcap into a USB port on your computer.
2. Go to Control Panel, click on the main heading: Hardware and Sound, then click Device Manager
3. In Device Manager, look under `Sound, video and game controllers." If you see "USB EMP Audio Driver" it needs to be changed.
(This is how to do that):
4. Right click `USB EMP Audio Driver' then `Update Driver Software'
5. Click `Browse my computer for driver software'
6. Click 'let me pick from a list .......'
7. Select `show compatible hardware'.
This should give you two driver options, Window's own `USB Audio Device' and the `USB EMP Audio Device' driver.
8. Select `USB Audio Device'.
9. Restart your pc and try using the ezcap again. It should work now.

There is one more little problem having to do with the arcsoft capture software thinking I'm trying to pirate copyprotected material (and I'm not, these are home videos). This happens when the tape has gotten warped for some reason (maybe it is bent in a certain location or has degraded over time) and the capturing process reads this as a copyprotection code. But I'm now trying another simple fix, just following the instructions of yet another buyer here on Amazon to edit an .ini file within the Arcsoft program. It is very simple to do and doesn't require any fancy software, just Notepad which comes with your Windows pc. The instructions are as follows: [NOTE: I changed the instructions to fit my location in the "Program Files (x86)" Folder. You may have to look under just "C:\Program Files\ArcSoft\Total Media ShowBiz\com.ArcSoft.CaptureModule\"

1. Navigate to:
C:\Program Files (x86)\ArcSoft\TotalMedia ShowBiz\com.ArcSoft.CaptureModule\

2. Open "CaptureModule.ini" with notepad. Add "ProtectOn=0" under "[CaptureModule]" and save.

If it does not let you save, it is because your pc user permissions need to be changed.
Right click on the file, select properties
select "security" at the top
click on "users" and click on the "edit" box
Put a click in all the boxes and click on "apply"

I'm enjoying seeing my old videos again, and now they are shareable on Facebook and Youtube. I encourage anyone with old magnetic tape formatted home videos to buy this and start saving them now. Yeah, there might be a slight learning curve, but you can do it, and this product does work. It would be nice if the manufacturers would start putting the answers into their packaging. I decided to give it Four Stars because of this, but otherwise it would rate 5.

review_title: Awful Customer Support -- Good Bluetooth Headset
review_text:
9/12/16 Update:
To put a bow on this review, I eventually did get a refund for the headphones, and Sol was kind enough to send me a free pair of headphones for my troubles.

In my initial review, I had forgot to mention that Sol double-charged me, which was also part of the frustrating customer service experience.

Because of Sol's making amends, I've added another star, but will still be leary of buying directly from Sol going forward.

-------------------

So 13 days after Sol Republic received my return, I am just now getting a refund. This is after basically calling Sol every other day, asking about the status of my refund. And I had to call from a different phone number, because for *some* reason, I could never get through to a customer service agent when using my phone, sometimes even getting sent straight to voicemail.

Bottom line: If you buy this, DO NOT BUY DIRECTLY FROM SOL REPUBLIC

10/15 UPDATE:
Sol Republic’s customer service is the worst. My return was received by Sol on October 8th, and a week later I still haven’t received my refund (or any kind of notification that it is coming soon).

I then call Sol’s customer support, who say they will call back me back soon with more details. Flash-forward 2 hours, still no call. So I sit on hold for 10 minutes and get kicked off, then again for 5 minutes. Still nothing.

So I dial *67 then Sol’s customer support #, and then miraculously they answer my call! What good fortune!

So to recap Sol’s poor customer service: it took them over 24 hours to email me back, then they didn’t refund me, and then they were obviously screening and not answering my calls. Just amazingly poor customer support.
-------------------

9/30 UPDATE:

So I gave these another shot – More or less the same experience, but this time I used them at my office job. It just wasn’t very practical to have one earbud in, and the other just hanging down the front of my dress shirt. And they didn’t stay on great – they would nearly slide off at times, since they didn’t have a good grip due to the fact that the headphones weren’t resting on my neck skin, but on my dress shirt.

Also, I didn’t have a great experience with Sol Republic’s customer support (this time I bought from their website due to coupon code). I emailed customer support, inquiring about their return process and I still haven’t received a response as of 24 hours later. I then called customer support, and they said they would email me a RMA form so I could ship my return, but as of 1 hour later I haven’t received any email from Sol Republic customer support. I guess I need to call them again...

I think these headphones are great for when you are able to have both earbuds in while wearing a tshirt/polo shirt/unbuttoned dress shirt, but they just aren’t practical for a corporate office setting.

product_name: FitDesk Under Desk Elliptical
review_text: Fits nicely under my corner desk where my computer sits and the gauge sits handily on my desk. Since I work at my computer a lot, I tend to keep my feet on the pedals and 3-5 times during my 8-hour day use it for periods of 10-15 minutes.  I have mild arthritis in my knees and fibromyalgia so to avoid overall joint pain, shorter sessions work best for me. Mostly I go for endurance (time) and don't worry much about distance or speed. It also helps with my overall fitness routine because I don't feel pressured to spend as much time on the treadmill or standing elliptical when I get home from work in the evening giving me time to do resistance training and still eat dinner at a reasonable hour.  And, on nights when I have an appointment after work and don't get home in time to work out, I feel like I've at least done something! This way, I can meet the recommendations for getting some exercise every hour in my sedentary desk job without interrupting my work flow and work to meet my overall fitness goals. (I still get up to stretch occasionally.)  I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for someone with really severe arthritis in their knees, but otherwise it should work for most people. (I also tried an under-desk bike and found it too hard on my joints.)  As others have noted, it did begin to squeak a bit after about a week, but a spray of pledge on the plates under the pedals stopped that. Overall, I think this has been a great purchase for me!
